labs.name: Neurorehabilitation Systems
labs.summary: Aalborg’s Neurorehabilitation Systems group develops interfaces that assist impaired sensory and motor function. Led by Strahinja Dosen, it studies prostheses, exoskeletons and functional electrical stimulation. The programme treats control and sensory feedback as complementary requirements for useful interaction between a person and an assistive device.
labs.approach: Myoelectric and brain-machine interfaces supply control signals, while haptic and electrical feedback can convey information about device state. Human experiments assess whether these loops are intuitive and usable. The group’s biomimetic approach connects physiological mechanisms with engineering choices, rather than assuming that technical accuracy alone predicts daily benefit.

projects.title: Semi-autonomous robotic prostheses
projects.detail: A current doctoral project running from 2026 to 2029 studies human-machine interfacing for semi-autonomous robotic prostheses. Dosen is listed among the supervisors. The registry establishes an active research direction, not completed performance results.

projects.title: Individualized assistive control
projects.detail: A 2025–2027 project investigates individualized, general-purpose myoelectric control of assistive technology, with Dosen participating. Related doctoral work on lower-limb sensory feedback distinguishes improvements in confidence and perceived control from less consistent biomechanical gains.

scale.detail: Control performance, cognitive load, confidence and physical task outcomes can move differently. Evaluating all of them is more informative than using a single signal-quality or electrode-count metric.

translation.detail: The group’s clinical motivation is clear, but project registry entries describe planned work. Findings from a particular feedback experiment should not be generalized to all prostheses or impairment groups.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: When does sensory feedback improve independent function beyond what a well-designed semi-autonomous controller already provides?
labs.affiliation: Aalborg University, Department of Health Science and Technology

labs.name: BrainGate — Brown Research Program
labs.summary: Brown’s BrainGate program develops interfaces that translate movement-related cortical activity into computer access, communication, and assistive control. It operates through a clinical collaboration rather than a single isolated laboratory. Brown lists Leigh Hochberg, John Simeral, and John Donoghue among its research leads.
labs.approach: The program records neural activity from intracortical arrays and decodes intended actions into commands for external devices. Engineering work includes wireless acquisition and reliable real-time systems, while clinical research asks whether participants with severe paralysis can use those commands for meaningful activities in their own environments.

projects.title: Wireless intracortical BCI at home
projects.detail: The 2021 study evaluated a percutaneous wireless recording system for home BCI use by people with tetraplegia. The transmitter attached to an existing skin-penetrating pedestal, so wireless data transfer did not make the system fully implanted.

projects.title: Assistive access and movement restoration
projects.detail: The broader BrainGate program develops cortical control of computer cursors, communication devices, robotic prostheses, and movement-assistance systems. Different studies address different functions and participant populations, rather than one device configuration proving every capability simultaneously.

scale.detail: The wireless study’s central advance concerns broadband acquisition and functional use beyond tethered laboratory setups. Long recording periods, successful control, and independence from researcher help should be tracked separately; they measure different aspects of translation.

translation.detail: The program aims to support people with spinal-cord injury, brainstem stroke, ALS, and other neurological impairment. Its research outcomes support further clinical development; a published demonstration is not a general treatment guarantee or proof of fully independent lifelong use.

labs.nextQuestion: Which parts of daily BCI operation still require assistance, and can those dependencies be removed without sacrificing signal quality or safety?

labs.name: N3 Neuroengineering and Nanophotonics Laboratory
labs.summary: Arto Nurmikko’s N3 lab studies both implantable neural microsystems and optical approaches to brain measurement. Its neurograin architecture distributes small wireless devices across the cortex, while a separate imaging program develops time- and space-resolved near-infrared methods for portable brain monitoring.
labs.approach: Neurograins combine sensing or stimulation circuitry with wireless power and communication. An external hub coordinates many small nodes, replacing a single large wired interface with a network. The hard problem shifts toward power delivery, addressing, shared bandwidth, packaging, and the ability to maintain useful signals from distributed sites.

projects.title: Distributed neurograin recording
projects.detail: The 2021 paper demonstrated individually addressed neurograins on a rat cortical surface for acute neural recording. Its distributed architecture targets sampling at spatially separated locations without routing a separate wire from each location.
projects.stage: Acute rodent demonstration and electronics development

projects.title: Higher-resolution near-infrared imaging
projects.detail: The lab describes development of a functional near-infrared spectroscopy system using space- and time-resolved methods. Portable monitoring and noninvasive BCI are proposed applications; this optical project is distinct from implanted neurograins and measures different biological signals.

scale.detail: The primary study demonstrated 48 neurograins in the acute rat preparation. Its potential scaling to 770 nodes came from link calculations and experimental characterization, not a demonstration of 770 implanted recording nodes or chronic human use.

translation.detail: Implantable neurograin work remains a research platform with packaging, communication, and biological validation requirements. The lab’s sensory-cortex projects include planned adaptation to nonhuman-primate experiments; planned applications should remain separate from completed recording results.

labs.nextQuestion: As the node network grows, which constraint fails first: delivered power, communication scheduling, chronic encapsulation, or the biological usefulness of additional sites?

labs.name: Andersen Laboratory
labs.summary: Richard Andersen’s laboratory investigates the transformation from sensory information to intended action, especially in posterior parietal cortex. Its neural-interface strategy emphasizes goals, grasp intentions, and decisions, alongside the lower-level trajectories needed by a robot. The program also develops functional-ultrasound approaches to decoding movement intentions.
labs.approach: Intracortical recordings reveal action potentials and field activity during cognitive and motor tasks. The group combines intention decoding with machine vision and robotic control, and separately studies learning, sensory stimulation, and awareness. Functional ultrasound offers another readout route through blood-volume changes associated with neural activity.
methods: Shared robotic control and machine vision

projects.title: Cognitive control of robotic devices
projects.detail: The laboratory develops algorithms that translate high-level intentions into cursor or robotic-arm actions in participants with tetraplegia. Machine vision and robot control can help execute an intended goal, making the allocation of control between person and machine an explicit design choice.
projects.stage: Human clinical research and robotics development

projects.title: Ultrasound decoding of movement intentions
projects.detail: The 2021 study examined single-trial decoding of movement intentions using functional ultrasound in nonhuman primates. This tests a hemodynamic readout rather than direct electrode recording; it should not be described as a demonstrated through-intact-skull consumer BCI.

scale.detail: Scaling can mean more useful intentions, broader image coverage, or lower setup burden. Ultrasound voxels, electrode channels, and independently decoded actions are different quantities and should not share a numerical growth curve.

translation.detail: The lab’s human implant research and preclinical imaging research have distinct evidence levels. Its clinical collaborations support neuroprosthetic studies, while imaging-based control needs separate evaluation of surgical access, latency, and generalization.

labs.nextQuestion: When should the person specify a goal and let a robot execute it, and when does that delegation remove useful control or agency?

sources.title: Single-trial decoding of movement intentions using functional ultrasound neuroimaging

labs.name: Biomedical Functional Imaging and Neuroengineering Laboratory
labs.summary: Bin He’s laboratory develops noninvasive methods to estimate brain activity, translate intended movement into commands, and modulate neural circuits. Its distinctive connection is between sensing and physical models: scalp measurements become estimates of distributed brain sources, while the same engineering program studies EEG-based robotic control and focused ultrasound.
labs.approach: The group combines EEG and MEG source reconstruction, anatomically informed models, deep learning, and human experiments. Its broader neuromodulation work investigates transcranial focused ultrasound in humans and animals; this is a separate intervention from decoding scalp EEG.
methods: Scalp EEG motor-imagery decoding with EEGNet
Deep-learning model fine-tuning with robotic feedback
signals: MEG and reconstructed cortical source activity

projects.title: Noninvasive robotic finger control
projects.detail: A 2025 study used subject-specific deep-learning models to translate executed or imagined finger movements into robotic-hand feedback. The online tasks distinguished thumb versus pinky, or thumb versus index versus pinky. Participants were able-bodied and already experienced with limb-level BCI; this was not independent simultaneous control of all fingers.

projects.title: Electrophysiological source imaging
projects.detail: The imaging program solves the inverse problem of estimating brain sources from EEG or MEG. Anatomical constraints, sparse signal processing, and machine learning support localization and estimates of source extent, with epilepsy research connecting those maps to presurgical evaluation.
projects.stage: Method development and clinical epilepsy research

scale.detail: In the 2025 finger study, 21 experienced users achieved mean motor-imagery accuracies of 80.56% for two-finger and 60.61% for three-finger classification after online training and fine-tuning. These are task accuracies, not numbers of independent neural channels.

translation.detail: The research connects noninvasive assistive control to clinical brain mapping. The finger experiment establishes laboratory feasibility; usefulness for people with paralysis and reliable everyday operation still require separate validation.

labs.nextQuestion: Can finger-level scalp decoding remain reliable across days and new users while source imaging helps choose informative features?

labs.name: Byron Yu Laboratory
labs.summary: Byron Yu’s group studies how populations of neurons jointly represent information and produce behavior. Rather than interpreting each neuron separately, it develops statistical descriptions of the lower-dimensional patterns shared across neurons. Brain–computer interfaces provide both an application for these models and a way to test how neural activity can be changed.
labs.approach: The work joins signal processing, machine learning, systems neuroscience, and collaborations with experimental neurophysiology groups. A latent state summarizes coordinated population activity; an online decoder or deliberately altered task then tests whether this representation predicts behavior and remains useful when recordings change.
methods: Factor analysis of neural population activity
Fixed Kalman decoding with adaptive signal stabilization
BCI tasks that challenge neural activity trajectories

projects.title: Stabilization through population alignment
projects.detail: A 2020 collaboration tested an adaptive stabilizer in two rhesus monkeys controlling a cursor. It aligned population representations before a fixed decoder and recovered control after imposed baseline shifts, unit dropouts, or tuning changes, without requiring the animal’s intended movement as a training label.

projects.title: Testing dynamical constraints
projects.detail: A 2025 study used BCI feedback to challenge monkeys to produce neural activity in unusual temporal orders, including reversing naturally observed trajectories. Difficulty violating those trajectories supported constraints imposed by neural population dynamics, making the interface an experimental probe of computation.

scale.detail: The 2020 study tested recovery across imposed instability conditions and multiple days. Its scale axis is robustness of population representations; it does not demonstrate indefinite stability of individual neurons or a growing human implant channel count.

translation.detail: These methods aim to reduce the recalibration burden of assistive BCIs. The selected experimental evidence is from nonhuman primates, and the dynamics experiments investigate circuit principles rather than demonstrate a clinical treatment.

labs.nextQuestion: Which population features remain stable when behavior, motivation, and the recorded neurons all change outside a constrained cursor task?

labs.name: Functional Neural Interface Laboratory — Tyler Lab
labs.summary: Dustin Tyler’s laboratory develops interfaces that restore sensation and function by connecting engineered systems to peripheral nerves. Its work emphasizes how a prosthesis feels and is used in daily life, alongside technical performance. Sensory restoration, neuro-inspired stimulation, and clinical implementation are central themes.
labs.approach: Sensors on a prosthetic hand measure contact and opening, and a stimulator translates those measurements into pulses delivered through nerve cuffs. In the studied home system, flat-interface nerve electrodes delivered sensory feedback while surface EMG controlled movement. The sensory and motor pathways therefore used different interfaces.

projects.title: Sensory-enabled prosthesis use at home
projects.detail: The 2018 study examined autonomous home and community use of a neural-connected sensory prosthesis in two participants. Outcomes included task performance, willingness to use the prosthesis, and experience of embodiment, rather than laboratory discrimination scores alone.

projects.title: Extending sensory interfaces across limb loss
projects.detail: The research program includes high-density peripheral nerve cuffs for lower-limb sensory restoration and stimulation strategies inspired by neural coding. This broadens the target beyond hand control while retaining the need to match stimulation to meaningful perception.

scale.detail: The home-use study occurred 41 and 42 months after cuff implantation. Those dates indicate implant age at testing, not uninterrupted home use for that duration. Prosthesis use and psychosocial benefit were measured separately from electrode counts.

translation.detail: The 2018 home system used an external stimulator and percutaneous leads; it was not fully implanted. Clinical translation therefore includes practical packaging and sustained usability as well as the quality of the evoked sensation.

labs.nextQuestion: What combination of natural sensation, reliable control, and manageable hardware actually increases long-term prosthesis use outside supervised studies?

labs.name: Bioelectronic Systems Lab (BIOEE)
labs.summary: Builds integrated circuits that combine sensing, processing, power delivery, and communication for electrical and optical neural interfaces.
labs.approach: The group moves functions onto a silicon substrate to reduce external wiring and make dense interfaces physically manageable. Its neural portfolio spans subdural micro-ECoG, implantable optical devices, and wearable near-infrared measurement.

projects.title: BISC wireless surface interface
projects.detail: The published device contains 65,536 electrode sites, with up to 1,024 recorded simultaneously. It integrates the analog front end, controller, wireless power, and radio. The paper validates the system in pigs and nonhuman primates.

projects.title: All-optical interfacing
projects.detail: The lab’s optoelectronic work combines single-photon detector arrays, microLEDs, filtering, and computational imaging. The engineering aim is to colocate optical measurement and stimulation in a thin device for neural-circuit experiments.

projects.title: Wearable time-domain imaging
projects.detail: Integrated nodes combine lasers, photon detection, and timing electronics for diffuse optical tomography. The cited circuit study includes a brain–skull phantom measurement; it is not a demonstration of cellular optical recording through a human skull.

scale.detail: BISC separates a large addressable electrode field from the subset that fits its wireless readout budget. The paper explicitly states that its in-vivo experiments did not demonstrate large-scale spiking activity from the surface recordings.

translation.detail: Animal recording duration and a mechanically compliant implant do not establish chronic human performance. Optical detector pixels, electrical sites, and concurrent channels are different units.

labs.nextQuestion: Would lower-bandwidth field-potential readout produce more useful simultaneous coverage than preserving spike-band capability at every site?

labs.name: Neural Prostheses Research Laboratory — Grill Lab
labs.summary: Warren Grill’s laboratory studies how electrical and magnetic stimulation recruit neural tissue and how stimulation can restore function. Its scope includes deep-brain stimulation, spinal-cord stimulation for pain, bladder control, vagus-nerve stimulation, and transcranial magnetic stimulation, making it broader than a recording-focused BCI laboratory.
labs.approach: The program combines models of electric fields and individual neurons with network simulations, animal physiology, and human feasibility experiments. Electrode geometry and pulse timing are both design variables. The laboratory asks which neural elements a stimulation pattern activates and whether that recruitment explains a clinically useful effect.
methods: Preclinical physiology and human feasibility studies

projects.title: Temporally optimized deep-brain stimulation
projects.detail: Computational optimization explores nonregular pulse sequences that can preserve therapeutic effects while reducing stimulation demands. The published work treats temporal pattern as an engineering variable, rather than assuming a fixed-frequency pulse train is the only option.
projects.stage: Computational, preclinical, and human feasibility research

projects.title: Neural control of bladder function
projects.detail: Peripheral recording and stimulation studies seek to restore continence and emptying. This work connects pelvic physiology with electrode design and recruitment models, involving clinical collaborators in urology and gynecology.
projects.stage: Translational research across models and human feasibility

scale.detail: Relevant scaling concerns include the useful effect achieved per stimulation dose, avoidance of unwanted recruitment, and robustness across anatomy. Adding contacts alone does not establish better control of symptoms or organ function.

translation.detail: The lab explicitly spans computational studies through clinical feasibility. Results from an optimized pattern or an animal bladder model require separate validation for the target patient population and stimulation hardware.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a model predict an individual’s therapeutic and off-target responses well enough to reduce trial-and-error programming?

labs.name: Viventi Laboratory
labs.summary: Jonathan Viventi’s lab uses flexible electronics to record cortical activity at fine spatial resolution across broad areas. It studies the hardware, packaging, and signal-analysis problems that arise when surface arrays become denser, with applications to epilepsy research, speech decoding, and general neural interfaces.
labs.approach: One engineering approach places amplifiers and multiplexers near recording sites to reduce the wiring burden. The program also develops flexible thin-film arrays for human and animal research and analyzes how densely cortical potentials need to be sampled. Device coverage, pitch, reliability, and usable information must be considered together.

projects.title: High-resolution speech recordings
projects.detail: The 2023 study recorded speech in four speech-abled neurosurgical patients using 128- or 256-channel micro-ECoG arrays. Millimeter-scale sampling helped distinguish speech-related activity during a brief non-word repetition experiment.

projects.title: Reliable broad-coverage surface electronics
projects.detail: The laboratory develops and tests flexible arrays, including active electronics that reduce one-wire-per-contact constraints. Parallel work evaluates fabrication repeatability, recording reliability, and spatial interpolation so larger coverage remains practically useful.
projects.stage: Device engineering and preclinical/clinical research tools

scale.detail: The speech experiment compared high-resolution recordings with coarser clinical modalities and used subsampling analyses. Its short intraoperative datasets do not establish chronic home use or free-conversation performance in a person with paralysis.

translation.detail: Human translation includes custom arrays deployed during indicated neurosurgery. The broader lab reports industry collaboration and licensing, while distinguishing usable research interfaces from the eventual goal of long-term therapeutic systems.

labs.nextQuestion: At a fixed connector and power budget, does closer spacing or coverage of another cortical region add more useful information for the intended task?

sources.title: High-resolution neural recordings improve the accuracy of speech decoding

labs.name: Courtine Laboratory / .NeuroRestore
labs.summary: The Courtine laboratory and its clinical collaboration investigate recovery after spinal cord injury and other nervous-system disorders. Engineering interventions connect intention, stimulation and rehabilitation, while animal experiments examine the circuits and cellular mechanisms that support recovery. Laboratory contacts are at Geneva’s Campus Biotech; clinical collaboration includes Lausanne.
labs.approach: Cortical recordings can control epidural spinal stimulation, replacing a disrupted communication pathway with an engineered link. Robotics and rehabilitation test whether this control helps meaningful movement. In parallel, genetically modified animals, optogenetics, viral tools and whole-brain imaging connect device effects with biological mechanisms.

projects.title: Brain–spine interface for walking
projects.detail: The 2023 Nature study linked implanted cortical recordings to epidural stimulation in one participant with chronic tetraplegia. The participant controlled standing and walking, including stairs and complex terrain. Reported stability over one year, including home use, is an individual proof of concept.

projects.title: Mechanisms of neurorehabilitation
projects.detail: The laboratory combines neuroprosthetics and robotic training with studies of neuroregeneration in rodent and primate models. Genetic and optical tools help identify which circuits contribute to motor recovery and which interventions might strengthen them.
projects.stage: Animal mechanistic research and translational development

scale.detail: The walking study’s one-participant, one-year observation is a concrete scale boundary. It does not establish population-level effectiveness or a general implant longevity estimate.

translation.detail: Clinical demonstrations motivate broader testing, but outcomes depend on injury characteristics, stimulation, rehabilitation and the complete implanted system. Brain–spine communication is one part of the programme.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which patient and circuit characteristics predict durable gains from combining intention decoding with stimulation and intensive rehabilitation?

sources.title: Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain–spine interface

labs.affiliation: EPFL, with CHUV and University of Lausanne

labs.name: Hummel Laboratory
labs.summary: The Hummel laboratory studies learning and recovery of sensorimotor function across healthy ageing and focal brain injury. Its neuroengineering programme asks how non-invasive stimulation can influence the networks needed for rehabilitation. Research sites include Geneva and Sion, linking behavioural experiments, imaging and clinically motivated intervention development.
labs.approach: Multichannel EEG, functional MRI and diffusion imaging characterize networks before and during intervention. The group uses temporal interference stimulation, transcranial electrical stimulation and multifocal magnetic stimulation, together with behavioural and clinical assessments. Target engagement and functional improvement are separate questions.

projects.title: Striatal theta-burst stimulation
projects.detail: A 2023 primary study investigated non-invasive theta-burst temporal interference stimulation of the human striatum. It combined motor-learning behaviour with imaging of striatal activity, providing a mechanistic human experiment rather than evidence of stroke-treatment efficacy.

projects.title: Personalized and home-use stimulation
projects.detail: The laboratory describes stimulation-based recovery research and a computer-vision approach to checking electrode placement for home tDCS in the DiSCoVeR depression programme. These address different translation problems: selecting a useful intervention and delivering it consistently outside the laboratory.

scale.detail: Useful measures include whether stimulation changes the intended network, whether learning improves and whether delivery remains consistent. They should not be collapsed into a count of recording channels.

translation.detail: Healthy-volunteer findings, stroke-recovery programmes and depression-related delivery work have distinct populations and stages. The laboratory homepage’s planned trials are not treated here as completed clinical evidence.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Can individualized stimulation parameters reliably improve recovery beyond training alone while maintaining accurate targeting during home use?

sources.title: Noninvasive theta-burst stimulation of the human striatum enhances striatal activity and motor skill learning

labs.name: Laboratory for Soft Bioelectronic Interfaces
labs.summary: Lacour’s laboratory designs electronics whose mechanical properties approach those of living tissue. The central engineering problem is maintaining useful electrical contact while the body bends, stretches and moves. At Campus Biotech, the programme connects soft-material fabrication, neural implants and controlled laboratory models of cell mechanics.
labs.approach: Microelectronics and MEMS processes are adapted to elastomers and other compliant substrates. Electrode geometry, stretchable conductors and encapsulation are considered together. The programme includes electrical recording, stimulation and chemical delivery, rather than treating flexibility as a stand-alone material property.

projects.title: Electronic dura mater
projects.detail: The 2015 e-dura collaboration developed a compliant implant integrating interconnects, electrodes and microfluidic chemical-delivery channels. Its mechanical endurance and multimodal operation illustrate how a tissue-like interface can accommodate repeated deformation. This is a historical research platform, not a statement of current clinical availability.

projects.title: Compliant peripheral and brainstem interfaces
projects.detail: The current research portfolio includes three-dimensional electrode interfaces for peripheral nerve repair and compliant surface electrodes for auditory brainstem implants. Related in-vitro platforms use controlled compliance to study cell biomechanics and guide device design.

scale.detail: Interface lifetime, strain tolerance and preserved electrical function provide useful measures of progress. The inspected sources do not provide a common electrode-count series across these designs.

translation.detail: The laboratory describes a path through in-vitro and animal testing toward human applications. Results for one soft implant should not be generalized to every intended nerve or brain target.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which combinations of soft materials, barrier layers and interconnect geometry preserve recording quality during years of tissue motion?

sources.title: Electronic dura mater for long-term multimodal neural interfaces
Neuroprosthetics for paralysis: a new implant on the spinal cord

labs.name: Bio Engineering Laboratory
labs.summary: Hierlemann’s Basel laboratory builds microelectronic tools to study living cells and neural networks. Its high-density microelectrode arrays make functional electrical measurements across cultured networks and tissue preparations. This is an important branch of neural-interface scaling, although the principal examples here are laboratory measurement platforms rather than human implants.
labs.approach: Microchips fabricated with cleanroom processes combine dense sensing with electrical access to neural tissue. Experimental preparations and analysis are designed together so that distributed activity, individual cellular signals and responses to intervention can be interpreted in context. Related department work connects these tools with drug testing and organ-on-chip systems.

projects.title: Reshaping cultured neural connections
projects.detail: A May 2026 ETH report describes a high-density array platform that selectively strengthens or weakens connections in rat cortical cultures. It presents a way to investigate network plasticity under controlled experimental conditions, without implying equivalent control of an intact human brain.

projects.title: Human retinal signalling
projects.detail: A January 2026 laboratory profile describes high-density array investigations of visual signalling and temporal coordination in human retinal tissue. It also distinguishes a prior collaborative retinal study from the researcher’s newly established work after returning to ETH.

scale.metric: Spatial coverage and identifiable electrical responses
scale.detail: Array density is useful when it improves separation and localization of biological signals. The sources do not establish one comparable neuron-count trajectory across cultured cortex and retina.

translation.detail: Commercial research instrumentation is one route from the laboratory, including the ETH spin-off MaxWell Biosystems. Ex-vivo human-tissue measurements are not clinical implant demonstrations.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: How can dense-array analysis distinguish altered synaptic connectivity from changes in excitability, cell health and recording geometry?

sources.title: Meet Annalisa Bucci: studying visual signaling in human retina

labs.affiliation: ETH Zurich, Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering

labs.name: Müller-Putz Team, Institute of Neural Engineering
labs.summary: The Müller-Putz team develops brain-computer interfaces for communication, movement and neuroprosthetic control. Its work connects non-invasive EEG decoding with the practical problems of reaching, grasping and receiving feedback. The wider Institute of Neural Engineering also has distinct cognitive and computational neuroscience teams.
labs.approach: Movement intention, trajectory information and error-related potentials provide different control signals. Functional electrical stimulation can turn decoded intention into movement, while sensory feedback closes the interaction loop. The group also studies implanted communication interfaces, which must be distinguished from its scalp-EEG work.
signals: Implanted cortical signals in development programmes

projects.title: NeuroGrasp
projects.detail: The project aims to improve EEG-triggered palmar grasp using movement-related cortical potentials and a stimulation neuroprosthesis. The team explicitly notes that earlier real-time control in people with spinal cord injury had excessive error rates, motivating improved machine learning and practical testing.

projects.title: Feel Your Reach and communication interfaces
projects.detail: The completed 2016–2021 Feel Your Reach programme combined intention, trajectory and error decoding with feedback. Separately, INTRECOM aims to develop fully implantable high-resolution communication BCIs for home use; that stated objective is not a demonstrated home-use outcome.
projects.stage: Completed EEG programme; separate implant-development aim

scale.metric: Reliable reach, grasp and error handling
scale.detail: Cross-session control, false activations and successful functional actions are useful comparison measures. The programme does not reduce to one electrode-count sequence across invasive and non-invasive projects.

translation.detail: The team’s reports make usability limitations visible, including error rates that impede neuroprosthetic control. Research ambitions for home communication require evidence at the complete-system and user level.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Can error detection and sensory feedback make EEG-controlled grasp reliable enough for daily use without imposing excessive attention demands?

labs.name: Computational Cognitive Engineering Lab
labs.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
labs.summary: Yiwen Wang’s lab treats a brain–machine interface as an adaptive partnership between neural populations and a learning controller. The group investigates how activity changes during learning and how information passes between cortical areas, with prosthetic control as an engineering application.
labs.approach: The work combines single-neuron recordings, computational descriptions of plasticity, and reinforcement learning. A distinctive direction is generating neural spike patterns from behavioral feedback, which could eventually help bridge a damaged information pathway when the desired downstream activity cannot be recorded.

projects.title: Behaviorally reinforced spike generation
projects.detail: A 2026 Nature Computational Science paper introduces a point-process model that turns upstream activity into spike trains by maximizing behavioral rewards. It avoids requiring healthy downstream recordings as supervised training targets.

projects.title: Adaptation across decoder settings
projects.detail: The same study tests adaptation and transfer across different decoder settings, asking whether generated movement-related spike patterns remain useful as the readout changes. This complements the lab’s broader work on learning and plasticity in motor interfaces.

scale.detail: The paper evaluates generated spike patterns, behavioral objectives, and changing decoders. It uses public data and previously collected rat data; these evaluations do not by themselves demonstrate recovery in a patient or a newly implanted stimulation experiment.

translation.detail: The authors identify neural prostheses and biomimetic cortical stimulation as future applications. The reviewed result is a model and evaluation framework with shared code, rather than an established clinical neural bridge.

labs.nextQuestion: What causal stimulation experiment would show that a behaviorally optimized spike generator restores useful communication between brain areas?

sources.title: A generative spike prediction model using behavioral reinforcement for re-establishing neural functional connectivity

labs.name: Neuromechanics and Rehabilitation Technology
labs.summary: The group treats spinal motor-neuron output as an accessible control signal for prosthetic limbs and rehabilitation devices. Instead of reading only a gross muscle envelope, it seeks the discharge timing of individual motor units from muscle recordings, connecting basic movement physiology to practical human-machine interfaces.
labs.approach: High-density surface EMG provides spatially distributed mixtures of motor-unit action potentials. Blind source separation and related decomposition methods estimate the underlying discharge trains. The programme also develops intramuscular electrodes, real-time hardware and stimulation strategies, so sensing, decoding and feedback are studied together.

projects.title: Real-time motor-neuron gateway
projects.detail: The research programme describes hardware that decomposes surface EMG in real time for feedback experiments, prosthesis control and rehabilitation. The spinal information is inferred through motor-unit recordings at muscle, rather than electrodes implanted directly into spinal neurons.

projects.title: Tremor monitoring and suppression
projects.detail: The team studies afferent stimulation to suppress pathological tremor. A 2022 primary study develops online tracking of phase differences between neural drives to antagonistic muscles, supplying information needed to time stimulation.

scale.detail: Motor-unit identification, robustness to electrode noise and real-time control performance are relevant measures. Electrode density alone does not establish prosthetic dexterity.

translation.detail: Bionic reconstruction work combines surgical nerve or muscle transfers with engineering. These projects span clinical collaboration and prototype control systems; the research pages do not certify general availability of each technique.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: How well do decomposed motor-unit commands remain usable after electrode repositioning, fatigue and changes in daily activity?

sources.title: Online tracking of the phase difference between neural drives to antagonist muscle pairs in essential tremor patients

labs.name: NeuRonICS Lab
labs.summary: NeuRonICS develops circuits and computing architectures that draw on neural computation and serve biomedical signal processing. The lab combines mixed-signal VLSI, probabilistic algorithms, and machine learning, with an emphasis on reducing the energy and memory needed close to a sensor.
labs.approach: Its biomedical program links high-density neural front ends to small inference engines for EEG, ECoG, intracortical signals, and EMG. The same systems perspective also appears in portable ultrasound, showing how acquisition physics and edge processing can be designed together.

projects.title: Compact neural decoding hardware
projects.detail: The lab lists a 2023 BioCAS study of a sparsity-driven tinyML accelerator for decoding hand kinematics in brain–computer interfaces. The engineering focus is performing useful inference within constrained computing hardware.

projects.title: SUSHRUT handheld ultrasound
projects.detail: The biomedical program describes a reconfigurable handheld ultrasound system combining nonlinear beamforming and edge AI. Related publications include the 2025 DOPCON double-pass convolution beamformer. This is an imaging-instrument program, not an invasive BCI.

scale.detail: The sources emphasize efficient on-device computation and acquisition quality. No single power figure, channel count, or imaging resolution is reported here because those quantities belong to different individual implementations.

translation.detail: Real-time neurorehabilitation and portable medical sensing motivate the biomedical work. The inspected program descriptions do not establish regulatory clearance or routine patient use.

labs.nextQuestion: How much energy can be saved without losing the information needed for reliable decoding when the neural signals change?

labs.name: BioNICS Lab
labs.summary: BioNICS designs the integrated circuits needed for compact neural interfaces. Its research spans recording front ends, on-chip classification, data compression, programmable stimulation, and security—components that determine whether a closed-loop implant can operate within power and communication limits.
labs.approach: The lab works at the circuit-to-system boundary. Instead of transmitting every raw sample, a device may extract features or detect a neural state locally; stimulation circuitry can then act on that decision. Reliable acquisition and protected communication remain part of the same system.

projects.title: Neural-tree classifier for feedback therapy
projects.detail: A 2025 IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems paper describes hardware optimization and implementation of a 16-channel neural-tree classifier for on-chip closed-loop neuromodulation. The number refers to classifier channels, not implanted participants or electrodes proven in a chronic clinical system.

projects.title: Acquisition and communication efficiency
projects.detail: The portfolio includes time-multiplexed front ends using chopping and autozeroing, neural-data compression, and a cryptographic security engine with sequence tracking. These tackle noise, bandwidth, and data integrity around the decoding block.

scale.detail: This is a defined processing-system metric from one publication. Future comparisons should also examine power, latency, detection errors, and the cost of acquiring and stimulating each channel.

translation.detail: Epilepsy and Parkinson’s disease motivate closed-loop implant designs. The sources describe engineering research rather than proof of disease-specific clinical benefit.

labs.nextQuestion: Which operations should remain on an implant so that feedback is fast and energy-efficient without hiding errors or reducing adaptability?

labs.name: Vestibular NeuroEngineering Laboratory
labs.summary: Charles Della Santina’s laboratory develops ways to restore useful inner-ear sensation for people with disabling balance loss. Its vestibular implant is a sensory prosthesis: motion sensors measure head rotation, and electrical stimulation communicates that motion through vestibular nerve branches so the brain can stabilize vision and posture.
labs.approach: The group combines engineering models, animal physiology, and human investigation. Gyroscope signals determine stimulation pulse timing and amplitude. Eye-movement measurements, balance tests, hearing assessments, and patient reports then test whether the nervous system uses the artificial signal effectively.
methods: Three-dimensional video-oculography and scleral search coils
Clinical posture, gait, hearing, and quality-of-life assessment
signals: Head angular motion measured by gyroscopes
Eye movements and vestibulo-ocular reflex behavior

projects.title: Motion-driven vestibular implantation
projects.detail: The 2021 clinical report studied unilateral implants in eight people with bilateral vestibular hypofunction. The device stimulated the three semicircular-canal nerve branches. Testing compared motion-modulated treatment with constant-stimulation placebo settings; several measures of posture, gait, and quality of life favored treatment.

projects.title: Patient-reported benefit over time
projects.detail: The expanded 2024 cohort report followed ten implant users, including the earlier eight, and compared them with ten applicants awaiting implantation. At six months, implant users reported improvements in dizziness, vestibular disability, and one health-utility measure; another utility instrument did not show a significant improvement. The groups were not randomized.

scale.metric: Useful sensation and durable everyday function
scale.detail: The key quantities are balance, gaze stability, hearing, disability, and follow-up time. Three stimulated semicircular-canal branches describe anatomical targets, not three decoded intentions or a count of individually controlled neurons.

translation.detail: The studies support clinical feasibility while exposing a material tradeoff: the 2021 report found hearing reduced in the implanted ear in all but one participant. Broader adoption requires evaluating benefit alongside hearing preservation and surgical outcomes.

labs.nextQuestion: Can stimulation selectivity and implantation technique preserve hearing while sustaining reliable balance and vision during everyday movement?

labs.name: Bio-Integrated Electronics and Systems Laboratory
labs.summary: Jeong’s lab makes soft electronic systems that fit the mechanical and practical constraints of living tissue. Neural devices combine flexible structures, wireless control, light delivery, and microfluidics; wearable systems extend the same engineering approach to physiological sensing and human–robot interaction.
labs.approach: The work joins materials and microfabrication with complete experimental systems. Softness alone is insufficient: a useful implant must also deliver power, route commands, and support repeated biological experiments. The group’s portfolio therefore includes networked control and automated neuroscience workflows as well as device materials.

projects.title: Networked neural pharmacology and optogenetics
projects.detail: The publication list includes a 2026 Science Advances study of an IoT-enabled wireless neural implant for chronic, programmable neuropharmacology and optogenetics. It combines different ways of perturbing circuits in one remotely controlled research platform.

projects.title: Wearable electrodes for exoskeleton control
projects.detail: A 2024 Science Advances paper reports stretchable microneedle adhesive patches for electrophysiological sensing and exoskeleton robot control without skin preparation. This extends biointerface engineering from implanted circuit experiments to wearable assistance.

scale.detail: The portfolio emphasizes tissue-compatible mechanics, chronic programmability, and reliable sensing. The overview does not provide a common channel or lifetime figure across these different devices.

translation.detail: The 2025 portfolio also includes AI and optogenetics research in male Parkinsonian mice. That animal context must remain explicit when discussing possible therapeutic uses.

labs.nextQuestion: When softness, wireless operation, and multiple stimulation modes are combined, which component limits reliable long-term operation?

labs.name: Brain Interfaces and Neural Prosthetics Laboratory
labs.summary: BINP investigates how engineered electric and magnetic fields activate nervous tissue. Its neuroprosthetic interests include vision, hearing, and deep-brain stimulation, with particular attention to microelectrodes and miniature coils that shape where stimulation acts.
labs.approach: The lab connects device geometry to the resulting neural response through computational field models and neurophysiology. This changes the central comparison from “how many contacts?” to “which neurons and cortical layers respond, over what area, and for how long?”

projects.title: Spatially selective magnetic stimulation
projects.detail: Lee’s research portfolio includes bent flat microwire arrays for selective activation of cortical columns and measurements of spatially confined mouse visual-cortex responses to microcoils. These publications establish a technical lineage that predates his move to KAIST in 2023.
projects.stage: Published preclinical work and continuing lab direction

projects.title: Propagation beyond stimulated cortex
projects.detail: A listed 2022 study examines focal, sustained secondary-visual-cortex activation after micromagnetic stimulation of primary visual cortex. The question is how local stimulation influences downstream processing, not just whether activity occurs near an implant.

scale.detail: Stimulation selectivity, cortical depth, and response persistence are central evaluation dimensions. The sources do not justify a single current implant-channel count or a patient-use claim.

translation.detail: Visual prostheses, cochlear implants, and deep-brain stimulation are target applications. The reviewed evidence supports mechanisms and device development; clinical effectiveness must be established for each eventual application.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a compact magnetic interface preserve spatial selectivity after packaging, implantation, and changes in surrounding tissue?

sources.title: Seungwoo Lee: faculty profile and key papers

labs.name: CashLab — Human Cortical Physiology Laboratory
labs.institution: Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School
labs.summary: Sydney Cash’s laboratory studies human cortical physiology across scales, from individual neurons to broader brain rhythms. Epilepsy, sleep, and transitions between brain states provide both scientific questions and clinical motivation. The lab connects advanced recordings with signal processing and models that could inform neurotechnology and treatment.
labs.approach: Much of the work uses clinical and research electrodes in people undergoing surgery for epilepsy or tumors. Combining spiking activity with local field potentials helps link cellular events to patterns visible at larger scales. This requires interpreting the surgical setting, brain state, and sampled tissue rather than treating every recording as typical healthy physiology.

projects.title: Human high-density single-neuron recording
projects.detail: The 2022 report introduced a modified Neuropixels probe and operating-room techniques for recording large cortical populations. It characterized diverse extracellular waveforms and relationships to events such as interictal discharges and burst suppression.

projects.title: Sleep, replay, and pathological network dynamics
projects.detail: The laboratory studies normal oscillations and seizure-related transitions. Its publication record includes learned motor-pattern replay during human sleep, connecting the temporal organization of neural populations to learning and to the design of future interventions.
projects.stage: Human systems and clinical neurophysiology research

scale.detail: The Neuropixels report described simultaneous recordings of more than 200 well-isolated cortical single units. This is an observed unit yield in acute human experiments, distinct from physical sites, acquisition channels, or chronic implant performance.

translation.detail: This research is embedded in MGH clinical neuroscience and the Center for Neurotechnology and Neurorecovery. Advanced research recording methods require their own workflow and regulatory evaluation; availability during an operation does not establish long-term implanted use.

labs.nextQuestion: Which cellular events reliably explain a clinically useful large-scale signal, and how much does that relationship change with brain state or pathology?

labs.name: Bioelectronics Group — Anikeeva Laboratory
labs.summary: Polina Anikeeva’s group engineers materials and devices for investigating communication between the brain and the body. Its work spans multifunctional fibers, gut–brain interfaces, and magnetic nanomaterials. The emphasis is on matching the mechanical and signaling complexity of living circuits rather than maximizing electrical contact count alone.
labs.approach: Thermal drawing creates flexible fibers containing electrical, optical, and fluidic functions. Brain and peripheral-organ probes require different mechanics, so the group integrates multiple components into systems suited to moving soft organs as well as brain tissue. Magnetic particles provide a separate route for externally triggered neural modulation.

projects.title: Wireless gut and brain fiber interfaces
projects.detail: The 2023 study integrated microelectronic functions into flexible fibers to record and modulate gut and brain circuits in mice. Light delivery and fluidic access support causal experiments on body-to-brain signaling during behavior.
projects.stage: Preclinical mouse research and device engineering

projects.title: Magnetic stimulation tools
projects.detail: The group develops injected magnetic nanomaterials that convert external magnetic fields into local stimuli. This can remove an implanted wire from the stimulation path, but particle delivery and biological targeting remain interventions that need validation.

scale.detail: A fiber may integrate recording, light, fluid delivery, and temperature measurement. Counting these functions is not equivalent to counting independently sampled neurons; useful scale includes stable organ access, causal specificity, and operation during natural behavior.

translation.detail: The current research program uses these tools to study brain–body circuits and develop future therapeutic approaches. Animal circuit manipulation and prospective treatment of human disease are different claims, especially when an approach requires genetic targeting or particle delivery.

labs.nextQuestion: Which combination of optical, electrical, and chemical access is necessary to identify a causal gut–brain pathway without changing the behavior being studied?

sources.title: MIT McGovern: Polina Anikeeva and brain–body research
Multifunctional microelectronic fibers enable wireless modulation of gut and brain neural circuits
MIT Brain and Cognitive Sciences: Polina Anikeeva research

labs.name: Synthetic Neurobiology Group — Boyden Laboratory
labs.summary: Edward Boyden’s Synthetic Neurobiology Group develops tools to measure, map, and control biological systems. Its portfolio includes optogenetics, expansion microscopy, and methods for multiplexing optical readouts. These technologies expand what researchers can observe or perturb, and need different metrics from implanted recording systems.
labs.approach: Expansion microscopy physically enlarges preserved specimens using a swellable material, allowing nanoscale structures to be studied with conventional light microscopes. Temporally multiplexed imaging instead separates signals in living cells by their distinct fluorescence dynamics. One increases spatial and molecular access in fixed material; the other increases separable live-cell measurements.
methods: Repeated antibody staining and image registration

projects.title: Multiplexed expansion revealing
projects.detail: The 2024 multiExR method used repeated staining and imaging of expanded specimens to map many proteins with nanoscale registration. Demonstrations included synaptic organization and Alzheimer’s-model mouse tissue, rather than live neural recording.

projects.title: Temporally multiplexed live-cell imaging
projects.detail: The 2023 TMI approach associates cellular signals with fluorophores having distinguishable time-dependent properties. Computational separation allows multiple dynamic signals to be recovered using a standard microscope, expanding beyond the usual restriction imposed by spectral colors alone.

scale.detail: multiExR mapped 23 proteins in an Alzheimer’s-model mouse-brain dataset. The number of proteins, effective spatial resolution, and round-to-round alignment error are separate measures; none is a count of simultaneously recorded neurons.

translation.detail: These are enabling research methods intended for broad adoption by other laboratories. Their use of ordinary microscopy infrastructure can reduce access barriers, but sample preparation, validation, and analysis remain substantial parts of the workflow.

labs.nextQuestion: How can increased molecular or temporal multiplexing preserve measurement accuracy and keep preparation and analysis practical for nonspecialist laboratories?

Multiplexed expansion revealing for imaging multiprotein nanostructures in healthy and diseased brain
Temporally multiplexed imaging of dynamic signaling networks in living cells

labs.name: neuroSPEED and MEG research program
labs.summary: Develops analysis methods, computational models, and open research infrastructure for large-scale brain electrophysiology.
labs.approach: The program links fast electrophysiological measurements to models of brain systems, combining MEG analysis with software and shared datasets. McGill’s MEG unit describes neuroSPEED as its own research laboratory alongside its core-facility role.

projects.title: Brainstorm analysis tools
projects.detail: The MEG unit contributes to Brainstorm, a collaborative open-source application for multimodal electrophysiology. Its practical role is to support analysis and interpretation of large datasets and make advanced workflows available to other researchers.

projects.title: Open MEG Archive
projects.detail: OMEGA is a McGill–Université de Montréal collaboration combining MEG, anatomical MRI, and participant information. The posted 3.1.1 release includes data from 644 participants and MEG–MRI co-registration for 480. Dataset size and registration completeness are separate measures.

scale.detail: For this program, the scale question includes participant diversity, recording coverage, co-registration, and reusable analysis. Dataset participants and source-localized brain activity are not equivalent to implanted channels.

translation.detail: OMEGA supports research through controlled access and a data-use agreement. MEG source estimates depend on modeling assumptions. McGill profile titles vary across pages, so this entry describes the documented research program rather than asserting a precise current faculty rank.

labs.nextQuestion: How robust are inferred network patterns when preprocessing, source models, and participant composition change?

sources.title: McGill — MEG unit and neuroSPEED research

labs.name: Monash Vision Group
labs.summary: Monash Vision Group develops a cortical visual prosthesis that converts camera images into patterns of electrical stimulation. The program combines visual neuroscience, miniature wireless electronics, implant packaging, image processing, and neurosurgical expertise.
labs.approach: The Gennaris architecture uses a wearable camera and processor to extract useful scene information before transmitting it to implanted tiles. A separate simulation environment helps evaluate how sparse flashes of light might support everyday actions and informs which visual information to preserve.

projects.title: Gennaris implant architecture
projects.detail: The technology page specifies up to 11 tiles with 43 microelectrodes each, giving a first-generation design capacity of 473 electrodes. Each tile contains receiver and stimulation circuitry. This capacity is not a count verified in a current human recipient.

projects.title: Testing useful visual representations
projects.detail: An iPhone and VR simulation explores object pickup, locating moving people, and obstacle navigation. These are simulation results based on assumed phosphene appearance, distinct from outcomes in an implanted person.

scale.detail: The figure is 11 × 43 across a proposed system. Perceptual quality also depends on electrode placement, activation selectivity, and the scene-processing strategy.

translation.detail: The group includes Alfred Health collaboration and reports preclinical evaluation. The inspected site describes preparation for first-human work; it does not establish a completed first-human outcome or lifetime implant reliability.

labs.nextQuestion: Which visual features deliver the largest functional benefit when only a limited, irregular pattern of phosphenes is available?

sources.title: Monash Vision Group: about and leadership

labs.name: Interactive Applications for Neuro-Rehabilitation Laboratory (LANR)
labs.summary: LANR builds interactive games and motion-sensing tools for motor and cognitive rehabilitation. Its interdisciplinary team turns exercises recommended by rehabilitation specialists into tasks that patients can practice with commercial sensors or custom interfaces.
labs.approach: The laboratory uses Unity alongside Kinect, Leap Motion, ergonomic pointing devices, and data gloves. Its stated pathway includes hospital evaluation and eventual home use with remote therapist follow-up. This makes engagement, exercise quality, and usable feedback central engineering issues.

projects.title: Charlie Escape: practicing hand opening
projects.detail: This Leap Motion game maps keeping the hand closed to forward movement and opening it to avoiding obstacles. The stated rehabilitation goals include grasping, pinch movements, and fine-motor control. The description establishes intended exercises rather than an effect size from a trial.

projects.title: Penal Madness and targeted arm movement
projects.detail: A Kinect-based goalkeeper game asks users to reach for shots and throw a ball with the hand and arm. Its listed targets include upper-limb flexion, extension, abduction, and adduction. Other games address finger pinch and visuomotor coordination.

scale.detail: Appropriate metrics include range of motion, accurate repetitions, and sustained participation. The reviewed pages describe applications and intended benefits but provide no controlled clinical outcome figures.

translation.detail: The team reports clinician consultation and hospital evaluation as part of development. Home rehabilitation and remote monitoring are stated goals; they should be distinguished from demonstrated routine deployment.

labs.nextQuestion: Does better game performance reflect recovery of the intended movement, and does that improvement transfer to daily activities?

labs.name: NeuroAI Lab
labs.summary: Libedinsky’s NeuroAI lab investigates the algorithms supporting attention, working memory, and decisions. It records individual neurons across macaque brain regions during cognitive tasks and relates those measurements to computational models and potential brain–machine interfaces.
labs.approach: A central problem is separating information that should be maintained from information that should update a memory. The lab’s tasks deliberately manipulate targets and distractors so that neural activity can be interpreted in relation to a specific cognitive operation, rather than a broad label such as “attention.”

projects.title: Updating versus protecting working memory
projects.detail: A Journal of Neuroscience study records lateral-prefrontal and prearcuate neurons while monkeys update remembered target locations and ignore distractors. The university advisor page labels an earlier version under review; the journal record establishes its publication.

projects.title: Learning in a BCI
projects.detail: The NUS research profile lists a 2022 Journal of Neural Engineering study of neural correlates of learning in a linear-discriminant-analysis BCI paradigm. This connects the lab’s interest in adaptive neural representations to an explicit decoding task.

scale.detail: The relevant scale is simultaneous neural-population information across cognitive conditions. No consistent current channel count or chronic implant lifetime is supplied by the inspected overview.

translation.detail: The program links basic cognition to computational intelligence and neural interfaces. Macaque memory mechanisms and experimental decoder learning do not establish a human memory-restoration device.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a decoder distinguish intentional memory updating from distraction when the same neurons participate in both?

Working Memory Updating in the Macaque Lateral Prefrontal Cortex
NUS Life Sciences Institute research profile

labs.name: Laboratory for Advanced Neuroengineering and Translational Medicine (LANTRN)
labs.summary: LANTRN develops minimally invasive ways to study and modulate neural systems throughout the body. Its engineering toolkit includes microdevices, materials, nanoparticles, and electroceuticals, with gastrointestinal applications showing how neuroengineering extends beyond the brain and spinal cord.
labs.approach: The laboratory connects device fabrication and wireless operation to biological access. A swallowed device can create an interface inside the digestive tract, but delivery of energy or information must still be matched to the particular cells and physiological process being studied.

projects.title: ICOPS wireless light capsule
projects.detail: A 2025 university report describes an LED capsule powered by magnetic induction and fabricated with 3D printing. It is designed for optogenetic experiments, which require the relevant neurons to be made light-sensitive; the source describes operation in freely moving animals.

projects.title: Tracking gastrointestinal motion
projects.detail: A 2023 collaboration describes a smart pill that senses externally generated magnetic-field gradients to infer its position and transmits measurements wirelessly. Tracking a pill’s passage offers a way to investigate digestive movement without assuming that the capsule directly records neurons.

scale.detail: The reviewed examples emphasize reaching the gut without implanted optical fibers and locating an ingestible sensor. No common electrode-count measure applies to these optical and tracking devices.

translation.detail: Digestive, metabolic, and neurological conditions motivate the work. The light-capsule result is an experimental optogenetic platform, not evidence that swallowing it alone treats a human disorder.

labs.nextQuestion: Can an ingestible interface identify and perturb the relevant gut circuit with sufficient anatomical and cell-type precision?

sources.title: Wireless light pill to control gut neurons

labs.name: Jackson Laboratory
labs.summary: Jackson’s research connects movement neuroscience with implantable interfaces, epilepsy and sleep. The programme explores how brain signals can guide stimulation below an injury and how abnormal cortical dynamics might be controlled. It includes engineering development, animal experiments and clinically connected rehabilitation research.
labs.approach: The work spans neural recordings, spinal stimulation and optogenetic control. Non-invasive studies use EEG, EMG, functional electrical stimulation and movement measurements. Keeping these modalities separate matters: a human rehabilitation experiment does not itself establish readiness of an implant or optogenetic therapy.

projects.title: Brain-to-spinal hand-function prosthesis
projects.detail: The university profile describes implantable electronics and surgical approaches for spinal stimulation controlled in real time by brain recordings. The intended application is restoration of hand function after spinal cord injury or stroke; the profile does not supply a clinical efficacy claim.

projects.title: CANDO and rehabilitation studies
projects.detail: CANDO pursued a cortical optogenetic implant for seizure control and a path toward human studies. Separately, the lab describes non-invasive upper-limb rehabilitation investigations in stroke and SCI using EEG, FES and movement measurements. CANDO’s stated trial ambition is not a verified trial outcome.
projects.stage: Preclinical translation; separate human rehabilitation research

scale.detail: Useful measures include the reliability of linking recorded signals to stimulation and longitudinal recording stability. The inspected pages do not establish a comparable channel-count trajectory.

translation.detail: Clinical goals are explicit, but sources describe different stages and include historical project pages. Human-use status must be checked at the individual project or trial level.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: How can stimulation reinforce useful motor plasticity without making control depend on fragile or drifting neural features?

sources.title: Andrew Jackson: Professor of Neural Interfaces

labs.name: Rogers Research Group — Bio-Integrated Electronics
labs.summary: John Rogers’ group develops soft, miniaturized electronics and microfluidic systems that can operate on or within living tissue. Its neurotechnology work belongs to a broader bioelectronics program spanning wireless devices, optical stimulation, physiological monitoring, and transient materials that dissolve after their useful period.
labs.approach: The engineering strategy combines compliant structures, biocompatible materials, microfabrication, and carefully controlled energy or fluid delivery. Instead of asking only how many signals can be recorded, these systems ask how to deliver a local intervention with less mechanical burden and, in some designs, avoid a second removal procedure.

projects.title: Bioresorbable nerve coolers
projects.detail: The 2022 project used a soft microfluidic device around a peripheral nerve to deliver localized evaporative cooling with temperature feedback. Reversible conduction block is a thermal intervention, distinct from electrically stimulating a nerve or releasing an analgesic.

projects.title: Implantable optical tools
projects.detail: The group develops miniaturized implantable light sources for optogenetic research. These devices deliver controlled illumination to genetically sensitized neural circuits, supporting experiments on circuit function without treating the light source itself as an autonomous therapeutic system.

scale.detail: Meaningful scale includes device footprint, spatial selectivity, feedback control, and useful operating lifetime. A device’s ability to dissolve is a design feature with its own timing and materials constraints, not evidence of long-term therapeutic effectiveness.

translation.detail: The coolers are research devices, with surgical pain management discussed as a possible application. The broader group’s clinical bioelectronics activities should not be used to imply that every neurotechnology prototype has reached human clinical use.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a transient device deliver a predictable therapeutic dose throughout healing while its material properties and tissue contact change?
