Dissolving implantable device relieves pain without drugs
Querrey Simpson Institute for Bioelectronics: institutional leadership and scope

labs.name: Slutzky Neuroprosthetics Laboratory
labs.summary: Marc Slutzky’s laboratory connects human-machine interfaces with recovery of movement and communication. A major branch is noninvasive rehabilitation after stroke: wearable muscle recordings provide feedback intended to reduce abnormal co-activation. Other branches investigate speech decoding and the effects of cortical stimulation used for clinical mapping.
labs.approach: The myoelectric interface for neurorehabilitation, MINT, trains people to activate muscles more independently. Home-based feedback is paired in current research with targeted memory reactivation during sleep. MRI, transcranial magnetic stimulation, and startle responses probe mechanisms rather than serving as interchangeable measures of treatment success.

projects.title: Home-based MINT after stroke
projects.detail: The 2021 feasibility study evaluated a wearable myoelectric interface for high-dose training in severely impaired chronic stroke survivors. Its central question is whether participants can train independently at home and improve abnormal muscle coordination.

projects.title: Sleep-supported learning and stimulation mapping
projects.detail: Current projects test whether sleep-linked memory cues enhance MINT conditioning in stroke survivors. A separate mapping program combines network analysis, cortical cooling, and calcium imaging to understand how electrocortical stimulation affects local and distant activity.

scale.metric: Training dose and transfer to daily movement
scale.detail: For this program, scale means accessible home practice, reduced pathological co-activation, and transfer to arm function. Better performance in an interface task is not automatically durable recovery in daily activities.

translation.detail: Wearable rehabilitation can avoid an intracranial implant, but still requires evidence about adherence and functional benefit. Speech-interface and stimulation-mapping projects have different participant populations and experimental access requirements.

labs.nextQuestion: Does improved muscle independence during home training persist after feedback is removed and transfer to useful reaching?

sources.title: Wearable myoelectric interface enables high-dose, home-based training in severely impaired chronic stroke survivors

labs.name: Neural Computation Unit
labs.institution: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology
labs.summary: Doya’s unit asks how brains learn and choose actions under uncertainty. It combines reinforcement learning and Bayesian inference with experiments on neuromodulators and adaptive robots, offering a route from biological mechanisms to algorithms that can be tested in embodied behavior.
labs.approach: The research organization explicitly spans theoretical models, rodent systems neurobiology, and robotics. Dopamine and serotonin are investigated as components of learning and decision-making, while computational projects ask how hidden neural states and model parameters can be inferred from measurements.

projects.title: Neuromodulators and decisions
projects.detail: The systems-neurobiology program studies how dopamine and serotonin participate in learning and choice. The important link is between a proposed computational role and measured behavior, rather than simply correlating one brain region with one task.

projects.title: Digital brains and reproducible analysis
projects.detail: The unit lists Brain/MINDS 2 Digital Brain and whole-brain data-assimilation projects, together with OptiNiSt and Neuro-Workflow analysis tools. These projects connect large models to experimental data and repeatable analysis pipelines.
projects.stage: Listed collaborative research and software programs

scale.detail: The current unit page lists Digital Brain for 2024–2030 and Fugaku whole-brain data assimilation for 2023–2026. These are project periods, not evidence that a complete human brain simulation has been achieved.

translation.detail: The primary outputs are explanatory models, analysis tools, and adaptive systems. Relevance to neuroengineering comes from better interpretation of neural data and more capable adaptive controllers.

labs.nextQuestion: Which learning rule explains both measured neural dynamics and behavior when the environment changes unexpectedly?

labs.name: Laboratory for Noninvasive Neuroengineering
labs.summary: Combines molecular engineering, focused ultrasound, and synthetic biology to access and monitor brain circuits without a permanent intracranial electrical interface.
labs.approach: The group engineers ways to deliver genes or drugs to selected locations and to report molecular states through blood sampling. This expands the meaning of a neural interface beyond an electrode or optical camera.

projects.title: Acoustically targeted chemogenetics
projects.detail: ATAC combines ultrasound targeting with gene delivery so that selected cells can subsequently respond to a chemogenetic actuator. The goal is spatial and cell-type selectivity without implanted intracranial hardware.

projects.title: Released markers of activity
projects.detail: Engineered reporter molecules link gene expression in the brain to measurements in blood. The lab’s publications distinguish synthetic serum markers from acoustically targeted measurement of transgene expression. These measure molecular state, not millisecond spike trains.

projects.title: Vector and delivery design
projects.detail: The lab describes viral-vector engineering and focused-ultrasound approaches for access across the blood–brain barrier. Delivery efficiency and the ability to repeat interventions are part of the platform-development problem.

scale.detail: The appropriate scaling questions concern distinguishable reporters, targeted regions, delivery coverage, and response dynamics. Serum-marker measurements cannot be compared directly with simultaneous electrophysiology channels.

translation.detail: “Noninvasive” here describes access strategies, not the absence of biological intervention: these programs can involve gene delivery and pharmacological control. The cited research does not establish a routine blood test for decoding human thoughts.

labs.nextQuestion: How many distinct molecular processes can be measured independently, and how does reporter transport blur their timing?

labs.name: Luan Laboratory of Integrative Neural Interface
labs.summary: Combines ultraflexible electrodes and optical measurements to study how neural populations change, recover after injury, and respond to precise stimulation.
labs.approach: The lab treats tissue integration as part of the measurement problem: a probe must keep useful contact with neurons while the tissue moves or reorganizes. Its research joins electrical recording, cellular imaging, and interventions across brain and spinal circuits.

projects.title: StimNET: selective, repeated activation
projects.detail: Ultraflexible intracortical electrodes were studied for low-threshold, spatially focused stimulation in mice. The work varies stimulus timing and amplitude while monitoring nearby neuronal responses; the intended application is more precise sensory prostheses.

projects.title: spinalNET during natural movement
projects.detail: A joint Luan–Xie and Salk study used compliant electrodes to record mouse spinal neurons during motor behavior. The aim is to retain recordings in tissue that deforms with locomotion and to relate spinal population activity to movement.

projects.title: Stroke and plasticity
projects.detail: The lab studies the relationship between neural function, blood vessels, inflammation, and recovery following injury, combining monitoring with open- and closed-loop modulation. This asks whether restored blood flow and restored circuit function follow the same trajectory.

scale.detail: Read the NET progression by configuration and biological setting. The separately documented 5,376-channel platform is acute rat surface micro-ECoG, not 5,376 chronically tracked single neurons. Stimulation selectivity and longitudinal recording stability need their own measurements.

translation.detail: The cited stimulation and spinal recording studies are preclinical. Visual restoration is a research direction; these sources do not establish a clinically available visual prosthesis.

labs.nextQuestion: If more contacts are added, does the number of independently controllable neural populations rise without sacrificing long-term stability?

sources.title: Rice — flexible nanoelectrodes and intracortical microstimulation
Rice — spinalNET in freely moving mice

labs.name: Mechatronics and Haptic Interfaces Lab
labs.summary: Develops robots, wearable sensing, and tactile feedback to measure and train human sensorimotor performance.
labs.approach: MAHI joins dynamic systems and control with human movement experiments. The important output is how people move, learn, and use their limbs, measured through the interaction between a person and an engineered device.

projects.title: Rehabilitation outside the clinic
projects.detail: The motion-assessment program develops lightweight hardware to track hand and wrist use and quantify movement. It distinguishes the ability to perform a clinic task from performance in everyday activities, aiming to inform therapist decisions.

projects.title: Learning with touch feedback
projects.detail: A mirror-tracing experiment uses a three-degree-of-freedom manipulator and a wearable vibrating bracelet. Feedback derived from speed or accuracy lets investigators study training strategies and retention after feedback is removed.

scale.detail: Useful measures include motion quality, actual daily use, and whether a skill remains after cues disappear. More sensors alone do not establish greater rehabilitation benefit.

translation.detail: The mirror task models elements of tool navigation; performance gains in that task do not by themselves establish improved surgical outcomes. At-home sensing is described as a research goal, not a replacement for clinical assessment.

labs.nextQuestion: Which feedback improves long-term independent performance rather than just performance while the device is assisting?

sources.title: Mirror tracing and real-time haptic feedback

labs.name: Nanoscale Neural Interface Laboratory
labs.summary: Engineers tissue-integrated neural electrodes and acquisition systems for dense, distributed, and longitudinal electrophysiology.
labs.approach: The central engineering strategy is to reduce the probe’s size and mechanical mismatch with neural tissue. The group combines ultraflexible structures, fabrication, optical assessment of tissue response, and system integration for recordings that persist over time.

projects.title: Tissue-integrated electrodes
projects.detail: The group uses ultraflexible electrodes and in-vivo imaging to examine integration with cells and capillaries. The lab reports recordings that track individual neurons over months; biological integration and signal continuity are linked design goals.

projects.title: Distributed recording at scale
projects.detail: The high-density program uses approximately 1 µm-thick structures and fabrication techniques intended to cover both local circuit volumes and distant brain regions. Device thinness is a physical dimension, not a recording-channel count.

projects.title: Acquisition and experimental throughput
projects.detail: A described SpikeGadgets collaboration targets tools for long-term recordings in large mouse and rat cohorts. Separately, the 2026 Luan–Xie–Chi platform provides 5,376 simultaneous channels at 20 kS/s with acute rat cortical surface validation.

scale.metric: Sites, concurrent channels, and stable units
scale.detail: Increasing the fabricated site count, the simultaneously digitized channels, and the neurons tracked over months are different achievements. The surface platform belongs on a separate series from penetrating NET arrays.

translation.detail: The acquisition project’s title mentions clinical research, but its stated development models are mice and rats. This profile does not reinterpret that title as a human implant demonstration.

labs.nextQuestion: Which limitation dominates next: insertion and packaging, concurrent readout, or maintaining the same useful neurons across months?

labs.name: Realtime Neural Engineering Laboratory
labs.summary: Builds real-time tools to investigate how hippocampal population activity supports learning, memory, and offline processing.
labs.approach: The lab combines recordings in behaving animals with online decoding and interventions. Detecting a neural event quickly enough to change it turns an observed correlation into a test of the event’s causal contribution.

projects.title: Closed-loop ripple experiments
projects.detail: The group develops detection and manipulation systems for hippocampal sharp-wave ripples during quiet wakefulness and sleep. Its project page links both a causal spatial-memory study and an open-source real-time ripple disruption system.

projects.title: Latent structure during sleep
projects.detail: Statistical decoding and latent-variable models seek structure in ensemble activity when overt behavior provides few labels. The 2024 Rice–Michigan work studied how rat hippocampal spatial representations change during post-experience rest.

projects.title: Reusable experimental software
projects.detail: The publication portfolio includes GhostiPy for signal processing and spectral analysis, and work on online clusterless decoding. These tools address data volume, reproducibility, and intervention timing.

scale.metric: Decoding latency and validated population structure
scale.detail: More simultaneous neurons are useful only if the system extracts reliable state estimates within the time needed for intervention. The lab’s sources support algorithms and causal experiments, not a single hardware-doubling series.

translation.detail: These sources describe memory experiments and research tools. Aspirations concerning traumatic memories are not evidence of demonstrated selective memory treatment in people.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a real-time decoder distinguish the content of a replay event well enough to perturb one hypothesis while preserving matched control events?

sources.title: Kemere Lab — publications and software studies

labs.name: Rice Brain Computer Interface Lab
labs.summary: Develops computational methods for reading intended movements and writing structured activity into neural circuits.
labs.approach: The lab connects motor-cortex decoding with population-level electrical stimulation. Its ambition is bidirectional interfacing: infer flexible actions from neural signals and select stimulation patterns that produce useful activity.

projects.title: Assistive robotic control at Rice and Baylor
projects.detail: In May 2026, Rice and Baylor announced joining BrainGate. Shah’s team develops decoding and robotic-control infrastructure, while Baylor provides clinical leadership. The stated focus includes coordinated actions for eating and drinking.

projects.title: Flexible motor representations
projects.detail: The lab presents BrainGate collaborator studies of attempted finger movements for typing and simulated quadcopter control. These results arose from collaborative work and should not be attributed solely to the newly established Rice site.

projects.title: Writing population activity in retina
projects.detail: The lab describes dynamically optimized stimulation and temporal combinations of simple stimuli in an ex-vivo retinal prototype. This studies the control of neural populations; it does not establish restored sight in a patient.

scale.metric: Controllable movement dimensions and population fidelity
scale.detail: Useful scaling measures include independently decoded movements, task performance, and how well stimulation reproduces target activity. The number of electrodes alone does not specify those capabilities.

translation.detail: The Rice lab opened in January 2025; the local BrainGate expansion was announced in 2026. Separate the human motor-decoding studies, the new clinical program, and the ex-vivo retinal work when comparing maturity.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a decoder support coordinated daily activities across changing contexts with less recalibration and assistance?

sources.title: Rice BCI Lab — projects, publications, and chronology

labs.name: Robinson Lab for Nano-neurotechnology
labs.summary: Builds miniature magnetic, electronic, and optical interfaces, alongside tools for observing neural circuits and behavior across species.
labs.approach: Magnetoelectric materials convert externally applied magnetic fields into electrical energy for small implants. A second thread co-designs optics and computation to collect neural and behavioral data with compact instruments.

projects.title: Distributed wireless bioelectronics
projects.detail: Miniature stimulators and implant networks aim to reduce batteries, wiring, and implant size. The lab’s cited studies include epidural cortical stimulators and endovascular peripheral-nerve stimulation. These are distinct anatomical delivery routes.

projects.title: Endocisternal access
projects.detail: The 2024 collaboration explores delivering interfaces through cerebrospinal-fluid spaces for brain and spinal recording or stimulation. Delivery route, implant placement, and electrophysiological access are the engineering contribution.

projects.title: NeuroAI measurement pipelines
projects.detail: Lensless microscopes and behavioral pipelines support large neural datasets. A cited 2024 study demonstrates mesoscopic calcium imaging in a head-unrestrained male nonhuman primate, broadening measurement beyond tethered electrode arrays.

scale.metric: Implant volume, wireless reach, and distributed access
scale.detail: Count independently powered and addressable implants alongside power delivery and recording or stimulation performance. For imaging, track field of view and behavioral freedom rather than electrode count.

translation.detail: Therapeutic targets described by the lab are development goals. The cited endocisternal and imaging work should be interpreted in their preclinical settings, not as evidence that the full portfolio is an established treatment.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a network of small implants gain coverage while maintaining reliable power, synchronization, and selective control?

labs.name: Tringides Lab — Cell and Material Technologies
labs.summary: Creates soft, electrically functional materials for conformable electrode arrays and laboratory models of nerves and neural disease.
labs.approach: The lab treats tissue mechanics as a design variable. Hydrogels with tunable electrical and viscoelastic properties support both implant structures and three-dimensional cultures that can be electrically measured.

projects.title: CHAMELEON arrays
projects.detail: Conductive hydrogel arrays are being developed with recording and stimulation electrodes. Matching both modulus and time-dependent deformation is intended to improve contact with curved, soft tissues. This remains a device-development program.

projects.title: hydroMEA nerve model
projects.detail: The 2026 Rice–ETH study combines human-derived sensory neurons, Schwann cells, hydrogels, channels, and high-density MEA measurements. It tested functional myelination through faster electrical propagation rather than relying on appearance alone.

projects.title: Neurons and glioblastoma in a controlled environment
projects.detail: A separate program places tumor cells and neurons in guided microstructures to observe invasion, interactions, and electrical activity while tuning the surrounding hydrogel.

scale.metric: Tissue compatibility and functional culture measurements
scale.detail: The hydroMEA report describes neuronal survival beyond 100 days. That is culture survival, not a 100-day implanted BCI result. CHAMELEON progress should be assessed through material and recording or stimulation performance.

translation.detail: Human-derived cells are not human clinical evidence. Both the nerve model and cancer platforms are tools to investigate mechanisms; clinical benefit from a hydrogel brain implant remains to be established.

labs.nextQuestion: Can electrode density increase while material mechanics, electrical isolation, and long-term tissue contact remain suitable?

labs.name: Brain-like Computing and Machine Intelligence: EEG and Affective Computing
labs.summary: The BCMI group studies how EEG and other physiological measurements reveal emotion, vigilance, and cognitive state. Its SEED dataset family is an important part of the research: experiments, labels, and benchmarks make algorithms comparable across people, sessions, and sensory contexts.
labs.approach: The group combines representation learning with experimental protocols for eliciting and labeling mental states. A major engineering issue is distribution shift: a classifier trained on one person, session, or culture may fail elsewhere. EEG restoration and domain adaptation address different parts of this problem.

projects.title: SEED emotion and vigilance resources
projects.detail: The lab distributes a collection of EEG-based datasets, including emotion, cross-cultural affect, olfactory stimulation, and driving vigilance. SEED-VLA explicitly addresses vigilance across different driving scenarios and participants.

projects.title: Restoring incomplete EEG
projects.detail: The university publication list includes STAR, a spatiotemporal autoencoder for EEG restoration, alongside studies of cross-cultural emotion adaptation. These projects ask how usable representations can persist when acquisition or participant characteristics change.

scale.detail: Dataset diversity and held-out participant performance are more appropriate measures here than electrode totals. The cited pages document multiple benchmark families; this profile does not combine their participants into a single experimental cohort.

translation.detail: Vigilance monitoring, affect-aware interaction, and mental-health research motivate the work. An EEG emotion label is an experimental construct, not a direct or infallible reading of a person’s private feelings.

labs.nextQuestion: Can an affect decoder distinguish a robust physiological correlate from a shortcut tied to a particular film, participant, or recording session?

sources.title: Bao-Liang Lu university profile and publications

labs.name: Brains in Silicon Laboratory
labs.summary: Kwabena Boahen’s group builds computing hardware inspired by neural biophysics. Its subject is efficient computation and models of brain circuits, rather than implantable electrode arrays. The lab connects transistor physics, circuit architecture, neuroscience, and the software needed to program analog hardware.
labs.approach: Mixed analog and digital circuits use device dynamics to implement neural computations, while event-based communication moves activity between components. The central question is how to obtain useful, programmable computation without paying the energy and data-movement costs of conventional arithmetic at every simulated time step.

projects.title: Neurogrid
projects.detail: The multichip Neurogrid platform emulates large neural populations with analog neural dynamics and digital communication. It provides a hardware substrate for investigating neural circuit organization and efficient large-scale simulation.

projects.title: Braindrop and hardware–software co-design
projects.detail: Braindrop links a mixed-signal neuromorphic architecture to a dynamical-systems programming model. The aim is to make heterogeneous analog circuitry usable through higher-level descriptions instead of requiring users to tune every device by hand.

scale.detail: Braindrop integrates 4,096 artificial neurons. These are circuit elements, not recorded biological cells or BCI channels. Useful scaling also depends on the supported computation, communication overhead, and the energy required to execute a task.

translation.detail: Stanford identifies the Brainstorm hardware–software effort and the 2018 Femtosense spinout as translation routes. This is a computing commercialization pathway, distinct from medical-device validation or demonstrated treatment of neurological disease.

labs.nextQuestion: Which biologically inspired dynamics remain useful when evaluated on an end-to-end workload that includes data movement and programming overhead?

labs.name: Neural Prosthetics Translational Laboratory
labs.summary: NPTL connects human motor and language neuroscience to assistive communication. The current laboratory identifies Jaimie Henderson and Frank Willett as co-directors. Its history includes Krishna Shenoy, who died in 2023; he should not be presented as a current director.
labs.approach: The team records intracortical population activity while participants with paralysis attempt movements or speech, then builds real-time decoders around those representations. Its research combines dimensionality reduction, neural dynamics, recurrent networks, and clinical system design. Automatic recalibration addresses changing neural signals between sessions.

projects.title: Attempted speech to text
projects.detail: The 2023 speech neuroprosthesis decoded attempted speech in a participant with ALS. The system combined neural decoding with language modeling, making communication speed and vocabulary-dependent error separate performance dimensions.

projects.title: Attempted handwriting and flexible movement control
projects.detail: The laboratory studies distributed movement representations and translates attempted handwriting into characters. Related finger-control research tests richer digital interaction, while calibration work asks how a learned mapping survives changes in the recorded population.
projects.stage: Human clinical research and algorithm development

scale.detail: The 2023 study reported 62 words per minute. That behavioral throughput must not be equated with electrode count, independent neurons, or error-free conversation; accuracy depends on the vocabulary and decoding configuration.

translation.detail: This is a BrainGate2 clinical-research program for people with severe motor impairment. Translation includes real-time use, signal drift, and participant priorities, rather than an established broadly available clinical product.

labs.nextQuestion: Can automatic adaptation preserve communication quality for months without requiring users to repeat lengthy calibration tasks?

sources.title: Stanford NPTL: leadership, research, and translation

labs.name: Neural Interfacing Lab
labs.summary: TUM’s Neural Interfacing Lab connects biological signal acquisition with models, robots and assistive devices. The MIRMI laboratory page identifies Melissa Zavaglia as senior scientist and describes a facility under development. Its distinctive contribution is an integrated experimental workflow across sensing, processing and device control.
labs.approach: The laboratory considers EEG, high-density EMG and neural implants as different inputs to an interface. Work includes sensor selection and in-vitro testing, placement methods, processing pipelines and stimulation. These activities are platform capabilities and research aims, rather than evidence that every modality has already been clinically validated there.

projects.title: Sensor-to-model experimental pipeline
projects.detail: The laboratory description covers selecting and testing sensors, placing them appropriately and extracting useful information from their signals. This provides a shared route for comparing interface options before connecting decoded information to an assistive system.

projects.title: Interfaces for neurodeficit assistance
projects.detail: The 2024 institutional profile links the lab with AI.D, Artificial Intelligence for Neuro Deficits, and describes brain-machine-interface research connected to robotic and assistive devices. The source names the initiative but does not report a clinical outcome or a finished commercial system.

scale.detail: A useful assessment follows the entire chain from sensing through decoding to assistive action. The institutional descriptions do not supply a comparable series of channel counts, control latencies or participant outcomes.

translation.detail: The programme is positioned to connect neuroscience and robotics. It should remain separate from TUM’s Neuroelectronics group, whose cited projects concentrate on device fabrication and cellular interfaces.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which sensing and decoding choices remain reliable when an assistive device must operate across changing tasks, body positions and users?

sources.title: Neural Interfacing Lab: research in the field of brain-machine interfaces

labs.name: Neuroelectronics Group
labs.summary: Wolfrum’s Neuroelectronics group engineers interfaces for recording and stimulating biological systems, including chemical as well as electrical communication. At TUM’s Garching campus, fabrication research connects printed electronics and sensor arrays with controlled cellular preparations and neural-interface development.
labs.approach: The programme uses structured cultures to make biological organization part of the experiment. Microchannels can orient axons, while localized lesions probe how network structure affects signalling and repair. Printed and three-dimensional electrodes address the geometry of tissue contact rather than simply expanding planar site counts.
signals: Activity in cultured tissue and organoids

projects.title: Three-dimensional interfaces for organoids
projects.detail: The laboratory’s 2024 publication list includes inkjet-printed three-dimensional electrode arrays for recording cortical organoids and laser-patterned epoxy arrays. These projects extend electrical access to three-dimensional preparations; organoid recording should not be described as a human implant demonstration.

projects.title: Structured networks and axotomy
projects.detail: The group develops microwire arrays for localized lesions and microchannels that guide axons, with a future goal of combined regeneration models. Its structured-network page also discusses cardiomyocyte experiments, which must be distinguished from the neuronal work.

scale.metric: Contact geometry and controlled biological access
scale.detail: Useful progress includes reaching three-dimensional tissue, localizing perturbations and interpreting chemical or electrical responses. The cited pages do not provide a consistent electrode-count history across these platforms.

translation.detail: The group spans in-vitro and in-vivo interface engineering. Research prototypes and public demonstrations do not by themselves establish clinical safety or therapeutic benefit.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Can printed three-dimensional interfaces improve longitudinal organoid measurements without changing tissue development or obscuring which cells generate each signal?

sources.title: Electrical and Computer Engineering research groups

labs.name: Neurotechnology / Berlin Brain-Computer Interface
labs.summary: TU Berlin’s Neurotechnology group develops brain-computer interfaces and human-computer interaction methods through advanced data analysis. Its current chair is Benjamin Blankertz. The Berlin Brain-Computer Interface provides historical and collaborative context, but old BBCI partner lists should not be treated as a current roster of European laboratories.
labs.approach: EEG sensing and machine learning connect experimental brain research with practical interfaces. An important engineering challenge is coadaptation: both the user and the algorithm change while the interface is being learned. Calibration design therefore matters alongside classifier accuracy.

projects.title: DAEDALUS coadaptation project
projects.detail: The graduate-school project on active learning for better user–BCI coadaptation investigates how sequential and active learning can reduce calibration burden. It considers information in EEG while users inspect stimuli, including signals that may be available before an explicit response.

projects.title: EEG sensing and decoding programme
projects.detail: The group’s research agenda joins sensor technology, detection of relevant brain patterns and machine learning. Its project archive also includes completed interface initiatives such as MindSee and BCI Live; those entries are historical projects, not evidence of ongoing recruitment or product availability.
projects.stage: Research programme; completed projects separately identified

scale.detail: Time needed to establish reliable control, adaptation across sessions and effective user interaction are meaningful measures. Increasing scalp channels alone does not demonstrate progress on these outcomes.

translation.detail: The programme can inform assistive access and broader human-computer interaction. Clinical effectiveness and product readiness need application-specific evidence beyond an institutional list of BCI projects.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Can active calibration reduce setup time without allowing user and decoder adaptation to reinforce misleading or unstable EEG features?

sources.title: DAEDALUS projects: active learning for better coadaptation of users and brain-computer interfaces

labs.name: Eldawlatly Neural Engineering Research
labs.summary: Eldawlatly’s university-described research uses signal processing and machine learning for invasive and noninvasive interfaces, visual prostheses, and neurological applications. This profile represents a faculty research program; the university page does not establish a separate formal laboratory name.
labs.approach: The work links algorithms to interface constraints: motor-imagery decoders must transfer between people, while prosthetic-vision processing must simplify a scene without discarding the information a user needs. The portfolio also includes EMG-based movement decoding and neural visual-encoding models.
signals: Visual images and neural visual responses

projects.title: Reducing motor-imagery calibration
projects.detail: A 2024 Journal of Neural Engineering study combines a modified VGG classifier with WGAN-generated spectral images. It evaluates transfer using leave-one-subject-out analysis on BCI Competition IV-2B, IV-2A, and IV-1, avoiding target-subject calibration data within that evaluation.

projects.title: Making images useful for prosthetic vision
projects.detail: The faculty portfolio lists PVGAN, a 2022 generative model for object simplification in prosthetic vision. This asks how to encode useful visual structure under a constrained display rather than assuming more image detail is always better.

scale.detail: The three-dataset evaluation is a reproducible algorithmic benchmark. It is not a count of prospective clinical trials, and benchmark transfer does not establish reliable daily operation for every user.

translation.detail: Assistive computer interaction and visual prostheses motivate the research. The reviewed evidence supports algorithm development, with clinical utility requiring separate prospective evaluation.

labs.nextQuestion: Will a calibration-free model remain reliable when the device, task instructions, and user population differ from the training benchmarks?

sources.title: AUC Seif Eldawlatly faculty profile and publications
Toward calibration-free motor imagery brain-computer interfaces: a VGG-based convolutional neural network and WGAN approach

labs.name: Gao Brain–Computer Interface Research
labs.summary: Gao’s research develops noninvasive brain–computer interfaces around visually evoked EEG, signal-processing algorithms, and usable interaction systems. It connects acquisition hardware to communication and robot control, making it a useful counterpoint to implant-centered neuroengineering.
labs.approach: The central design problem is extracting an intentional command from weak scalp recordings while controlling the visual stimulation and feedback that generate those recordings. The wider Tsinghua program connects this work with language neuroscience, brain networks, and intelligent medical instrumentation.
methods: Joint spatial, temporal, and frequency feature extraction

projects.title: High-speed visual spelling
projects.detail: The university profile describes a 2015 spelling interface that combined visual stimulation and decoding to reach 267 bits per minute. This is a historical task-specific information-transfer result, not a general-purpose neural bandwidth measurement.

projects.title: EEG-guided robotic interaction
projects.detail: The research portfolio includes high-frequency visual BCI combined with computer vision for robotic-arm control, alongside vigilance estimation and neurofeedback. These projects connect neural commands with additional sensing and interactive software.

scale.detail: The cited 267 bits/min result belongs to the 2015 spelling experiment; the profile also records a 64-channel EEG acquisition system used in a 2010 competition. Channels and information-transfer rate measure different things.

translation.detail: Communication and assistive control are application directions. The sources establish research systems and publications; they do not establish unsupervised clinical deployment.

labs.nextQuestion: How much communication speed survives when stimulus fatigue, calibration time, and operation outside a laboratory are included?

labs.name: Neural Computation Laboratory
labs.summary: The laboratory studies how dendrites, synapses and circuit connectivity transform inputs into neuronal output. Its current UCL page lists Beverley Clark, Arnd Roth and honorary professor Michael Häusser. Cerebellar and neocortical experiments provide a tool-development perspective that complements device-focused BCI laboratories.
labs.approach: The group combines cellular electrophysiology, optical measurements and anatomical analysis. Its distinctive emphasis is identifying which individual synaptic inputs and dendritic mechanisms produce a circuit-level computation, rather than interpreting a population recording without testing the underlying connections.

projects.title: All-optical synaptic plasticity
projects.detail: A 2025 collaboration combined JEDI-2Psub voltage imaging with selective granule-cell activation in awake mice. Pairing granule-cell activity with sensory-evoked climbing-fibre inputs altered inhibitory responses in Purkinje cells, allowing defined synaptic effects to be probed during behaviour.

projects.title: Dendritic and cerebellar computation
projects.detail: The ongoing laboratory programme uses the structured cerebellar circuit and neocortex to connect cellular properties with network function. It asks how dendrites transform synaptic inputs and how connection patterns contribute to information processing.

scale.detail: The 2025 optical experiment reports imaging at 440 Hz over specified small fields. This is imaging throughput and voltage sensitivity, not an electrode or neuron-count doubling series.

translation.detail: These tools support causal circuit investigation in animals. The cited experiments do not demonstrate a clinical BCI or a treatment for human learning disorders.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Can optical read-write measurements follow identified synapses across learning while separating plasticity from changes in behavioural state?

sources.title: All-optical voltage interrogation for probing synaptic plasticity in vivo

labs.name: Neuroengineering Group, Institute of Biomedical Engineering
labs.summary: The University of Buenos Aires identifies Sergio Lew as responsible for its Neuroengineering Group, whose listed themes include neural networks and bioprosthetics. The surrounding biomedical institute investigates neural signals, rehabilitation, and engineering methods for restoring lost function.
labs.approach: The institute’s neuroscience program studies frontal, motor, and dopaminergic neuronal signals in animal models. A complementary human-recording example applies information-theoretic analysis to intracranial EEG, connecting engineering measures of network dynamics with observable changes in consciousness.

projects.title: Neural signals for interfaces and neuroprostheses
projects.detail: The institute describes studies of frontal, motor, and dopaminergic neurons as a foundation for interfaces intended to restore function. This is a documented research direction; the page does not identify a completed implanted prosthesis or a current channel total.

projects.title: Information dynamics during seizures
projects.detail: Lew’s 2024 Argentine neuroscience meeting abstract describes an integrated-information measure applied to stereo-EEG from six people with refractory epilepsy. The analysis compares interictal, preictal, and ictal periods and reports correlation with a consciousness scale.

scale.detail: The six-person count belongs only to the conference abstract, not the group’s total clinical experience. The abstract is narrower evidence than a complete peer-reviewed methods and results article.

translation.detail: The research connects neural measurement and modeling to interface design and clinical interpretation. The reviewed sources establish a group and research examples, with limited public detail on intervention outcomes.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a network measure predict a clinically meaningful state in unseen recordings, independently of seizure artifacts and recording location?

sources.title: SAN 2024: Neural activity and behavior in vertebrates; Sergio Lew abstract

labs.name: Muller Lab
labs.summary: Designs low-power integrated circuits and wireless systems for implantable neuromodulation and wearable electrophysiology.
labs.approach: The lab works at the intersection of electronics and physiology: amplifiers, sensing, stimulation, local processing, and wireless links must fit within the same power and artifact constraints.

projects.title: WAND: recording while stimulating
projects.detail: WAND digitizes 128 recording channels on board; the reported radio streams 96 channels in open-loop mode. Up to eight stimulation channels can operate concurrently. Onboard artifact cancellation and biomarker detection enable closed-loop control, addressing the problem of stimulation obscuring the signal used to guide it.

projects.title: Wireless ear EEG
projects.detail: The ear-EEG work develops dry electrodes in a user-generic earpiece and a lightweight wireless interface. It tackles the practical fit and acquisition requirements of a low-profile wearable, rather than increasing intracortical access.

scale.metric: Useful channels within a power and artifact budget
scale.detail: Keep onboard acquisition, radio throughput, and stimulation concurrency separate. WAND’s closed-loop radio stream contains two channels plus calculated spectra; artifact cancellation interpolates contaminated samples. Ear EEG instead emphasizes wearable form factor and signal quality.

translation.detail: The group’s institutional portfolio includes multiple device classes. A closed-loop research demonstration does not validate every therapeutic target named in the broader research vision, and wearable EEG records a different signal scale from implanted electrodes.

labs.nextQuestion: How much reliable information can be preserved per unit of power after accounting for stimulation artifacts and wireless transmission?

sources.title: WAND: wireless artifact-free neuromodulation — final paper

labs.name: UC Davis Neuroprosthetics Laboratory
labs.summary: The UC Davis Neuroprosthetics Lab is co-led by neuroscientist Sergey Stavisky and neurosurgeon David Brandman. It focuses on restoring speech and language while using the same human recordings to understand how movement and communication are represented in neural populations.
labs.approach: The program combines chronic Utah-array recordings with short-term Neuropixels studies. Its engineering spans surgical access, real-time processing, machine learning, and user-facing communication. Crucially, rapid conversion of attempted speech into text and direct synthesis of voice solve related but different problems.

projects.title: Rapidly calibrated speech communication
projects.detail: A 2024 study in one participant with ALS reported a speech-to-text system suitable for self-paced conversation after brief training. Evaluation included extensive vocabulary and use with family and colleagues, alongside explicit single-participant limitations.

projects.title: Instantaneous voice synthesis
projects.detail: The 2025 brain-to-voice system decoded neural activity into audible speech in real time. It addressed the delay and limited expressivity of systems that wait for a complete sentence before speaking it aloud; data and implementation code were shared.

scale.detail: The 2024 paper reports 97.5% accuracy during self-paced conversations and more than 248 cumulative hours across 8.4 months after implantation. Cumulative use is not uninterrupted recording, and the result concerns one participant.

translation.detail: The program combines neurosurgery and longitudinal assistive use within clinical research. Generalization to additional users, disease progression, and reliable everyday voice output remain separate questions from the success of the reported demonstrations.

labs.nextQuestion: Can low-latency expressive voice remain dependable as ALS and the neural recording change, without trading away the user’s control of timing?

sources.title: UC Davis Health: Neuroprosthetics Lab and current investigators
An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis

labs.name: Neuroelectronics Lab
labs.summary: Combines transparent neural electronics with optical measurement and develops device technologies for energy-efficient neural computation.
labs.approach: Transparent graphene interfaces allow electrical recording and optical observation of the same tissue. The group also studies emerging memory and quantum-material devices for computation, connecting measurement hardware with neuro-inspired electronics.

projects.title: Surface recordings paired with cellular imaging
projects.detail: In transgenic mice, a transparent high-density graphene array was paired with calcium imaging beneath the cortical surface. Models learned relationships between the two measurements to predict deeper calcium activity from surface potentials.

projects.title: Cortical–hippocampal interactions
projects.detail: The group’s Neuro-FITM work combines flexible, insertable, transparent electrodes with multimodal observations to investigate interactions between cortex and hippocampus. This extends the portfolio beyond purely surface measurements.

projects.title: Devices for neural computation
projects.detail: The laboratory investigates nonvolatile and quantum-material devices, including phase-change and resistive memory, through device–algorithm co-design. These devices perform computation; they are not recording electrodes or biological neurons.

scale.metric: Joint electrical–optical coverage and prediction quality
scale.detail: The 2024 study’s 20 µm electrode diameter and imaging depth up to 250 µm describe geometry and validation conditions. Prediction at depth must be assessed separately from direct measurement at depth.

translation.detail: The surface-to-depth result is model-based inference validated against calcium imaging in mice. It should not be described as direct deep-brain spike recording or established human BCI performance.

labs.nextQuestion: How well does the electrical-to-optical relationship transfer across days, behavior, and brain states that were absent from model training?

sources.title: UC San Diego — Duygu Kuzum research profile
UC San Diego — transparent implant and depth prediction

labs.name: Translational Neuroengineering Lab
labs.summary: Integrates neural recording, real-time systems, and statistical learning to develop and test neural prosthetic systems.
labs.approach: The lab’s posted research portfolio combines clinical electrophysiology, animal models, and embedded-system design. It moves between understanding signal representations and engineering systems that can use them online. The biography was updated in 2021; reviewing these pages in 2026 does not confirm that every listed project remains active.

projects.title: Neuron channel compression
projects.detail: The project page identifies heat and power as bottlenecks for growing electrode arrays. Its proposed channel-compression work aims to reduce output dimension while retaining latent neural dynamics. That is an engineering objective, not a demonstrated lossless-compression guarantee.

projects.title: Responses beyond intended movement
projects.detail: Clinical sEEG and ECoG recordings during games or tasks are used to study non-volitional responses as potential inputs to intelligent controllers. This broadens the interface beyond a direct mapping from an attempted movement to an actuator.

projects.title: Songbird vocal prostheses
projects.detail: The group develops multichannel recording and algorithms linking neural activity to vocal production in songbirds. A university profile identifies a jointly advised Gilja–Gentner project aimed at an animal model for future speech-prosthesis development.

scale.detail: Compression should be evaluated against neural-dynamics fidelity, downstream task performance, and real-time constraints. Fewer output channels alone cannot establish that all useful neural information was retained.

translation.detail: The portfolio contains different evidence streams: clinical recordings, animal vocal models, and proposed algorithms. A songbird prosthesis is not itself a human speech-restoration result.

labs.nextQuestion: Can dimensionality reduction preserve rare, behaviorally important signals that contribute little to average population variance?

sources.title: UC San Diego — songbird prosthesis project
TNEL — institutional contact and group identity

labs.name: Chang Laboratory
labs.summary: Edward Chang’s laboratory studies how human cortical circuits perceive and produce speech, and uses that knowledge to develop communication neuroprostheses. It also investigates functional mapping that helps surgeons preserve language, connecting basic human neurophysiology with both restorative technology and safer brain surgery.
labs.approach: The lab combines psychophysics, local field potentials, microelectrode recordings, cortical stimulation, and real-time signal processing. High-density cortical recordings resolve spatial and temporal patterns associated with articulation, which can be translated into text, acoustic features, and facial movements rather than treating speech as a single classification problem.
methods: Neural speech synthesis and avatar control

projects.title: Speech, synthesized voice, and avatar control
projects.detail: The 2023 study used a participant’s cortical activity to produce text and audiovisual speech outputs. Separate models converted neural activity into phoneme sequences and sound features, with synthesized speech also driving a personalized facial avatar.
projects.stage: Human clinical research in a participant with paralysis

projects.title: Speech representation and language-preserving mapping
projects.detail: The laboratory investigates the circuits underlying speech perception and production using recordings and stimulation during human research. This foundational work informs which cortical features should be decoded and which language-critical areas should be preserved during surgery.
projects.stage: Human systems neuroscience and surgical mapping research

scale.detail: A meaningful comparison includes vocabulary, text accuracy, synthesized-speech intelligibility, and audiovisual timing. These are different outputs of the interface; combining them into one electrode-count ranking would hide the lab’s principal technical contribution.

translation.detail: The speech neuroprosthesis is clinical research, while language-preserving mapping connects to neurosurgical practice. The 2023 result demonstrates capabilities in its studied participant and configuration, rather than population-wide treatment effectiveness.

labs.nextQuestion: How can a speech interface maintain intelligibility and a user’s expressive identity across spontaneous conversation and long-term signal changes?

sources.title: Chang Lab: foundations of human speech and research methods
A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control

labs.name: Bioelectronics Laboratory
labs.summary: This materials-led laboratory develops electronics that make close, mechanically compliant contact with neural tissue. Its neuroengineering programme links organic electronic materials to surface recordings and improved implant longevity. The group is relevant to BCI scaling because electrode density becomes useful only when the tissue interface preserves signal quality.
labs.approach: Organic electronic interfaces connect ionic biological signals with electronic readout. The programme combines conformable microelectrode arrays, transistor-based recording and work on tissue compatibility. Its current Cambridge identity should be distinguished from earlier collaborative NeuroGrid work performed before Malliaras moved to Cambridge.

projects.title: Conformable cortical arrays
projects.detail: The laboratory reports ultra-conformable arrays capable of recording cortical activity, including surface single-neuron recordings in epilepsy patients. The linked NeuroGrid paper provides the earlier material and recording rationale; it is a historical collaboration, not a newly announced Cambridge clinical device.

projects.title: Active recording and durable interfaces
projects.detail: A second direction uses transistors to record brain activity while improving contact between electronics and tissue. High-density arrays and interface-longevity strategies are stated development priorities; the lab overview does not supply a clinical lifetime or a uniform channel-count series.

scale.detail: The meaningful comparison is stable surface signal capture under conformal contact, not a count of probes. These sources do not establish a laboratory-wide doubling rate.

translation.detail: Human recording experience supports translational relevance, while chronic therapeutic benefit and implant lifetime require separate evidence. The neuroengineering page states goals, not general clinical availability.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which material and packaging changes preserve single-unit surface recordings as array area and implantation duration increase?

sources.title: NeuroGrid: recording action potentials from the surface of the brain

labs.name: Neuroengineering Research Laboratory (NER Lab)
labs.summary: NER Lab studies how neural commands, muscles, and biomechanics interact to control human movement. It combines computational neuroscience with human neurophysiology, seeking mechanistic explanations that can eventually inform restoration of motor function during disease and aging.
labs.approach: The laboratory connects cellular and motor-unit dynamics to observable force, posture, and electromyograms. This is a different engineering scale from cortical recording arrays: a model must explain how many physiological components produce the same measurable movement.

projects.title: Multiscale modeling of ALS-related motor changes
projects.detail: A featured project models how altered motor-neuron dynamics associated with ALS could influence muscle force and EMG. The source describes a theoretical program supported by grants from the 2010s; it should not be read as a newly completed clinical diagnostic system.

projects.title: Shared neural drive across calf muscles
projects.detail: Another featured project uses high-density EMG and decomposition to compare motor-unit synchronization in soleus and gastrocnemius during plantar flexion and upright posture. Force and joint position help test contributions from voluntary commands and proprioception.

scale.detail: The important outputs are synchronization, force variability, and agreement between model and experiment. The source does not supply a common participant total or electrode count for these distinct projects.

translation.detail: The lab aims to translate basic motor-control knowledge into rehabilitation methods. Its research descriptions support mechanisms and tools, without establishing clinical efficacy for a particular intervention.

labs.nextQuestion: Can a model distinguish changes in descending neural drive from changes in muscle mechanics when both alter the same EMG and force measurements?

sources.title: Leonardo Elias biography and current role

labs.name: Meintjes Neuroimaging Research and CUBIC
labs.summary: Meintjes’s research develops and applies MRI methods to understand brain development after early-life exposures and disease. The program connects imaging engineering with questions especially relevant to South African populations, including prenatal alcohol exposure and HIV-related influences.
labs.approach: The work combines structural imaging, diffusion measurements, functional connectivity, and methods for tracking and correcting motion during scanning. A major engineering challenge is obtaining reliable measurements in children and separating biological differences from motion and other measurement effects.

projects.title: Connectivity and arithmetic after prenatal exposure
projects.detail: A 2024 paper examines resting-state connectivity around five parietal seeds involved in number processing in 57 children. It relates prenatal alcohol exposure, connectivity, and arithmetic performance, providing an example of imaging linked to a concrete cognitive outcome.

projects.title: Improving the measurement itself
projects.detail: The university describes Meintjes’s work on tracking and correcting motion during MRI, alongside studies of prenatal exposures, HIV, and brain development. These methods address a practical obstacle to interpreting pediatric scans.

scale.detail: The 2024 study includes 38 children with fetal-alcohol-spectrum exposure categories and 19 controls. This is one study’s cohort, not the size of CUBIC or the university’s overall imaging program.

translation.detail: Imaging can help characterize mechanisms and evaluate developmental outcomes. An observed connectivity association is not by itself a diagnostic test or proof that an intervention changes cognition.

labs.nextQuestion: How much apparent developmental difference remains after motion, exposure history, and other sources of measurement bias are controlled?

labs.name: Brain-Computer Interfaces and Neural Engineering Laboratory
labs.summary: Essex’s BCI-NE laboratory combines assistive communication, neural decoding and cognitive-state monitoring. Its current university roster identifies Caterina Cinel and Ian Daly as co-directors. The programme covers both non-invasive and invasive interfaces, with practical emphasis on interpretable signals and systems usable beyond a carefully controlled experiment.
labs.approach: EEG acquisition, adaptive machine learning and biosignal modelling support communication, movement-intention decoding and mental-state estimation. Research also covers dry electrodes, sensory feedback and stimulation. The laboratory’s broad remit should not be mistaken for a single implant product or a uniform clinical pipeline.

projects.title: PaiNeuro objective pain measurement
projects.detail: The 2025–2028 project links Essex’s EEG processing and machine-learning expertise with clinical pain-management expertise at Vestre Viken Hospital Trust. Its aim is to investigate neurophysiological measurements for pain assessment; a diagnostic accuracy or validated clinical test is not reported here.

projects.title: Assistive and cognitive BCIs
projects.detail: The group develops communication and control interfaces alongside systems using neural and behavioural information to support individual or group decisions. These are distinct applications: assistive access, rehabilitation and cognitive augmentation require different outcome measures and user populations.
projects.stage: Human BCI research and technology development

scale.detail: Generalisation, calibration requirements, portability and end-user control are more informative here than a cumulative laboratory electrode count.

translation.detail: Clinical collaboration and accessible hardware are priorities. The institutional page does not make every listed research direction a validated therapy or an available assistive product.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Can adaptive decoders preserve interpretable, reliable decisions when EEG quality, user strategies and real-world tasks change together?

labs.name: Laboratory for Biomedical Microtechnology
labs.summary: Stieglitz’s laboratory develops the physical interfaces and packaging needed to connect electronics with the nervous system. Its programme emphasizes flexible electrodes, assembly and reliability. This makes it particularly relevant to the gap between a functioning experimental array and a system that can withstand long-term use in tissue.
labs.approach: Polyimide and silicone interfaces are fabricated using microsystems and laser-based techniques. Electrical testing is combined with mechanical deformation, accelerated ageing and structural inspection. System integration adds telemetry, feedthroughs and encapsulation, making the complete device rather than an isolated electrode the unit of engineering.

projects.title: Flexible long-term electrode structures
projects.detail: The electrode-interface programme lists FlexBRM research on long-term polyimide thin-film shafts. Its wider methods evaluate how stimulation, repeated deformation and ageing affect interfaces, with in-vitro and in-vivo testing serving different validation roles.

projects.title: Distributed electronics and packaging
projects.detail: The system-integration programme studies conformally encapsulated micro-ASIC networks, capacitive telemetry, ceramic housings and miniaturized feedthroughs. Flexible cables and chip-in-foil approaches address how active electronics can be connected while maintaining a mechanically compatible system.

scale.detail: Failure mechanisms, packaging integrity and preserved electrical function are more informative than electrode count alone. Accelerated ageing is evidence about tested conditions, not a direct guarantee of a clinical lifetime.

translation.detail: The laboratory explicitly addresses assembly and regulatory translation. The inspected project descriptions do not establish approval or human effectiveness for every component or architecture.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which failures dominate after flexible electrodes, interconnects and packaging are assembled into a complete implant, and how well do bench tests predict them?

labs.name: NeuroBionics Laboratory
labs.summary: Melbourne’s NeuroBionics Laboratory develops interfaces, stimulation methods, and medical devices that connect nervous-system measurements to useful actions. The research spans endovascular and subscalp electrodes, electrical and ultrasound stimulation, and assistive control systems.
labs.approach: The laboratory works across device fabrication, electrophysiology, signal analysis, and feedback control. Its public project list is especially useful for seeing how a neural-interface platform can serve different physiological targets, rather than treating every application as another cursor-control demonstration.

projects.title: Intravascular interface engineering
projects.detail: The research page describes fabrication and investigation of Stentrode-related intravascular interfaces, alongside subscalp electrodes and long-term recording and stimulation. These projects concern access routes and stability as well as the decoding algorithm.

projects.title: Feedback for rehabilitation and autonomic control
projects.detail: The current people page lists projects on BCI biofeedback for stroke rehabilitation and automatic closed-loop urinary-bladder control with a Stentrode. These are distinct proposed feedback applications; the listings do not report completed therapeutic outcomes.

scale.metric: Access route, stability, and feedback performance
scale.detail: The overview supplies no common channel count across endovascular, subscalp, and stimulation systems. Comparison should use each project’s recording stability and physiological or behavioral control endpoint.

translation.detail: The lab targets practical medical devices and rehabilitation, with current projects spanning movement and autonomic function. A listed research project is not proof that its intended clinical function is already available.

labs.nextQuestion: Which sensing route gives sufficiently stable information for a feedback controller that must operate through changing physiology?

labs.name: Cortical Neural Prosthetics Laboratory
labs.summary: Cynthia Chestek’s laboratory develops brain and peripheral interfaces for restoring hand movement. Its research spans cortical decoding, carbon-fiber electrodes, and regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces, allowing comparison of two distinct access routes: recording brain activity or using reinnervated muscle to amplify residual motor commands.
labs.approach: The group combines electrode fabrication and tissue evaluation with online prosthesis control. In regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces, a severed nerve reinnervates a small muscle graft; implanted electrodes then record its electromyographic output. This is biological signal amplification, rather than direct recording of every axon in the nerve.
methods: Implanted EMG and online prosthesis control

projects.title: RPNI control of artificial hands
projects.detail: The 2020 pilot investigated regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces in four people with upper-limb amputation, with prosthesis-control tasks in two. Reinnervated muscle provided usable signals for real-time hand control, including continuous thumb movement.

projects.title: Small carbon-fiber interfaces
projects.detail: The lab develops arrays of very small carbon-fiber electrodes and evaluates recording yield and surrounding tissue. This line of work addresses whether reducing the physical footprint can support stable neural access while retaining a manufacturable, implantable array.

scale.detail: The RPNI paper includes real-time prosthesis control up to 300 days without control-algorithm recalibration in one participant. This is a task-specific stability result, not a claim that all grafts or all degrees of freedom were followed equivalently.

translation.detail: RPNI work is conducted with surgical, rehabilitation, and prosthetics collaborators. The reported study was a small, nonrandomized pilot; cortical electrodes and carbon-fiber interfaces follow different development and clinical-validation paths.

labs.nextQuestion: When a prosthesis fails outside the laboratory, is the limiting factor graft signal stability, electrode mechanics, decoder drift, or the control scheme?

sources.title: A regenerative peripheral nerve interface allows real-time control of an artificial hand in upper limb amputees

labs.name: Willsey Lab for Brain-Computer Interfaces
labs.summary: Matthew Willsey’s laboratory studies implantable interfaces to restore movement and communication in people with severe disabilities. A distinctive emphasis is dexterous finger control and the activities participants actually want to do, including digital recreation, rather than evaluating a decoder only through generic cursor tasks.
labs.approach: The group turns neural activity into continuous finger commands, using real-time machine-learning models and tasks that test independent control. This separates the number of physical electrodes from the number of movement variables a person can control. Preclinical decoder studies and human clinical demonstrations provide complementary evidence.

projects.title: Human finger decoding and virtual quadcopter control
projects.detail: A 2025 study in one participant with spinal-cord injury decoded three finger groups, including two-dimensional thumb control, for four degrees of freedom. The decoded finger commands controlled a virtual quadcopter through obstacle courses.

projects.title: Fast continuous finger decoding in primates
projects.detail: The 2022 work tested a shallow feedforward neural-network decoder for high-velocity prosthetic finger movement in nonhuman primates. This is an online control experiment, rather than an offline prediction benchmark or a human treatment result.

scale.metric: Independent control dimensions and task throughput
scale.detail: The human study reports four decoded degrees of freedom and an average acquisition rate of 76 targets per minute in its finger task. A degree of freedom is a controlled movement variable, not an electrode or neuron.

translation.detail: The lab’s official site describes active clinical studies and first-in-human Connexus research. Those device studies should be tracked separately from the published finger-decoder experiment, whose findings concern one participant and a specified task.

labs.nextQuestion: How much additional independence does another controllable finger variable provide once fatigue, task preference, and daily setup are included?

labs.name: Aplin Group: Electrical Neuromodulation
labs.summary: Aplin’s group studies the biological effects of electrical stimulation, particularly in peripheral nerves and pain pathways. It combines experimental neurophysiology with device engineering to understand why a waveform activates or suppresses particular fibers and how disease changes that response.
labs.approach: The approach measures responses to meaningful sensory inputs and realistic stimulation patterns. Ionic direct-current delivery, peripheral nerve recordings, muscle responses, and spinal assays address different steps between an electrical command and a functional biological effect.

projects.title: Suppressing naturally evoked pain-pathway activity
projects.detail: A 2024 study applied direct current to the sciatic nerve and recorded spinal responses to natural hindpaw stimuli in rat models of neuropathic and inflammatory pain. It found reductions in noxious-evoked activity, providing preclinical evidence for further development.

projects.title: More precise functional electrical stimulation
projects.detail: The group investigates how sensory and motor axons respond to single, repetitive, burst, and kilohertz stimulation. Human and rat electrophysiology tests assumptions about translating pulse trains into predictable neural and muscular output.

scale.detail: The central comparison is which sensory or motor responses change, rather than the number of implanted contacts. The pain study records evoked spinal activity; it is not a demonstration of durable pain relief in patients.

translation.detail: Pain treatment and functional restoration motivate the program. Disease-dependent responses and the gap between physiological suppression and patient benefit remain important evaluation boundaries.

labs.nextQuestion: Can stimulation suppress the unwanted signal while preserving the sensory and motor functions a person still needs?

sources.title: Peripheral direct current reduces naturally evoked nociceptive activity at the spinal cord in rodent models of pain

labs.name: Bioelectronic Circuits and Systems / Denison Group
labs.summary: Denison’s programme builds physiological feedback into neurotechnology. It brings microelectronics, control theory, clinical neuroscience and health economics together to create instruments for early human studies. The practical goal is useful treatment functionality within healthcare constraints, not merely a more complex implant.
labs.approach: Sensing circuits and algorithms are integrated with implantable stimulation or non-invasive instruments. The work studies how physiological state should change treatment parameters and how a prototype can fit existing clinical pathways. Oxford explicitly places much of this work at technology-demonstration readiness.

projects.title: Physiology-responsive smart implants
projects.detail: The team develops central and peripheral stimulation systems whose control can respond to physiological measurements. The institutional profile describes instruments for first-in-human neuroscience and translation; it should not be read as proof that every proposed controller has established clinical benefit.

projects.title: EPIONE chronic-pain engineering
projects.detail: The programme beginning October 2025 combines implantable and non-invasive stimulation research for chronic pain. Tim Denison and Ben Seymour lead the multidisciplinary effort, with engineering approaches studied alongside clinical neuroscience rather than a single device architecture.

scale.detail: Oxford identifies improvement in patient outcomes relative to deployment cost as a translation criterion. This complements signal fidelity and controller performance.

translation.detail: Clinical and industry partnerships support proof-of-concept testing. Technology demonstrations and proposed therapies remain distinct from regulatory approval or established NHS adoption.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which sensed states justify changing stimulation, and does the resulting benefit outweigh controller complexity and clinical support costs?

labs.name: Litt Lab — Translational Neuroengineering
labs.summary: Brian Litt’s research connects clinical epilepsy with implant engineering and computational analysis of brain networks. The program asks both how to measure disease-related activity more effectively and how that information could guide intervention. Litt is identified by Penn as director of the Center for Neuroengineering and Therapeutics.
labs.approach: The engineering approach combines electrode hardware, signal analysis, network neuroscience, and clinical recordings. The examples below show two complementary routes: increasing spatial sampling through local electronics, and extracting temporal organization from signals already collected during epilepsy evaluation.
methods: Active amplification and multiplexing at the array

projects.title: Flexible multiplexed cortical mapping
projects.detail: In a foundational 2011 collaboration, flexible silicon transistors were integrated with a cortical electrode array to reduce wiring demands. Cat experiments mapped sleep spindles, visual responses, and electrographic seizures, including recurrent spiral-wave patterns. This was animal cortical mapping, not a chronic human BCI demonstration.

projects.title: Dynamic seizure networks
projects.detail: A 2015 collaboration analyzed presurgical ECoG from 21 people with neocortical epilepsy. Time-varying connectivity separated seizure states and examined how strong and weak connections reorganized during seizure generation and termination. The work proposed circuit-targeting relevance; it did not establish that an intervention based on these maps prevents seizures.

scale.detail: The 2011 device contained 360 recording channels and 720 silicon transistors. Transistors are circuit components, not additional neural channels. The separate network study’s 21 patients are a cohort count, not simultaneous recording capacity.

translation.detail: Penn’s center connects engineering and medicine to develop restorative and therapeutic devices. The selected studies establish hardware and analytical foundations; clinical benefit, long-term implant reliability, and prospective decision performance are distinct translation questions.

labs.nextQuestion: When does finer spatial sampling change the stimulation or surgical decision enough to improve a patient’s outcome?

labs.name: Rehab Neural Engineering Labs — Sensorimotor Interfaces
labs.summary: Pittsburgh’s Rehab Neural Engineering Labs bring together investigators developing rehabilitation technologies around motor control and sensation. Robert Gaunt and Jennifer Collinger are current faculty central to the sensorimotor-interface work. Historical touch collaborator Sliman Bensmaia was at the University of Chicago and died in 2023, rather than being a current Pittsburgh lab leader.
labs.approach: The sensorimotor program pairs decoded motor commands with artificial sensory feedback. A robotic hand’s interaction with an object can drive stimulation of somatosensory cortex, allowing users to receive information that vision alone does not provide. Related research examines how stimulation recruits spinal, ganglion, and peripheral circuits.

projects.title: Touch feedback during robotic-arm control
projects.detail: The 2021 study combined a motor BCI with intracortical stimulation that evoked tactile sensations. It tested whether adding that feedback improved manipulation, treating sensory information as part of a closed control loop rather than a stand-alone percept demonstration.

projects.title: Recruitment and restoration beyond the cortex
projects.detail: Gaunt’s program investigates stimulation in spinal cord, dorsal-root ganglia, and peripheral nerves, including approaches intended to restore bladder function after spinal-cord injury. These mechanistic questions differ from decoding voluntary hand movement.

scale.detail: Relevant outcomes include manipulation performance, reliable sensory localization, and the contribution of feedback during contact. More motor recording channels do not by themselves measure how much usable tactile information a participant receives.

translation.detail: RNEL connects engineering with rehabilitation and clinical research. Different projects address people with paralysis, basic recruitment mechanisms, or future restorative therapies; they should not be combined into one claim of clinical maturity.

labs.nextQuestion: Which sensory features must a prosthesis convey for confident everyday manipulation, and which can be simplified without reducing useful control?
