labs.name: Rehabilitation Engineering Laboratory
labs.summary: Investigates electrical stimulation, neuroprostheses, and sensorimotor control for recovery from neurological motor impairment.
labs.approach: Located at UHN’s KITE Research Institute and connected to the University of Toronto, REL supports multiple research groups. Its website identifies Kei Masani as director and Milos Popovic as founder. The program joins rehabilitation experiments with engineering models and devices.

projects.title: Functional electrical stimulation therapy
projects.detail: A 2022 multicenter randomized study compared FES therapy delivered with MyndMove against conventional therapy in incomplete tetraplegia. Both groups improved, and the authors reported comparable effectiveness; this should not be rewritten as clear superiority of the device.

projects.title: Balance training and user experience
projects.detail: A case-series program combined FES with visual feedback for standing balance. A related qualitative study interviewed five participants about confidence, daily activity, and continuing rehabilitation, adding context that quantitative balance tests may miss.
projects.stage: Human case series and qualitative study

scale.metric: Function, balance, and meaningful daily activity
scale.detail: Track retained functional improvement and user experience alongside laboratory movement measures. Study dose, baseline impairment, and comparator therapy affect the interpretation of gains.

translation.detail: The randomized study notes pandemic-related enrollment and protocol disruption, baseline differences, and variation in conventional therapy across sites. The five-person interview study provides experience evidence, not a population efficacy estimate.

labs.nextQuestion: Which laboratory improvements predict sustained changes in everyday independence, and how should participant priorities shape the endpoints?

labs.name: Clinical Neurophysiology
labs.summary: Twente’s Clinical Neurophysiology group uses engineering and clinical neuroscience to improve diagnosis and treatment of central nervous-system disorders. EEG is central to its work on epilepsy, ischaemia and intensive-care monitoring. Close links with Medisch Spectrum Twente connect physiological questions with clinical decisions.
labs.approach: Electrical measurements are interpreted with computational models and experimental perturbations such as magnetic stimulation. The programme also studies neuromodulation, including spinal cord stimulation for pain and vagus nerve stimulation for epilepsy. Its scope spans monitoring and intervention, so evidence should be assessed separately for each application.

projects.title: EEG biomarkers of epileptiform activity
projects.detail: A July 2026 study analysed two-channel subcutaneous EEG in ten people with pharmacoresistant epilepsy, with 14–16 days assessed per patient. Mean-field model parameters and spectral slope showed associations with epileptiform discharge occurrence, while a waveform-derived candidate did not. These are candidate biomarkers, not established treatment rules.

projects.title: Monitoring vulnerable brain states
projects.detail: The clinical programme studies EEG changes associated with cerebral ischaemia and recovery, including intensive-care neuromonitoring. Computational work asks how neural mechanisms generate observed EEG, helping connect signal features with the physiological states clinicians need to distinguish.

scale.detail: The biomarker study combines two channels with multi-day recordings in ten patients. Longitudinal coverage and robust physiological interpretation can matter more here than increasing channel count.

translation.detail: Clinical partnerships make the research directly relevant to practice. A candidate biomarker or feasibility study remains distinct from a validated decision rule and from proof that changing care improves outcomes.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which EEG features remain reliable enough across sedation, injury and individual physiology to support actionable bedside decisions?

sources.title: Candidate EEG-derived biomarkers of epileptiform discharge occurrence in epilepsy

labs.name: Restorative Technologies Laboratory
labs.summary: Develops stimulation and neuroprosthetic strategies to improve movement after spinal cord injury or stroke.
labs.approach: The group studies both bypassing damaged pathways and making spared circuitry more useful. Its program connects physiological experiments, device development, and rehabilitation with human participants.

projects.title: Hand and arm function after spinal injury
projects.detail: A multicenter 2024 study combined noninvasive cervical stimulation with rehabilitation in people with chronic tetraplegia. The university account describes an initial rehabilitation-only phase followed by stimulation-assisted training, with heterogeneous outcomes.

projects.title: Walking, recovery, and circuit repair
projects.detail: The lab investigates skin-surface spinal stimulation with exercise or robotics for standing and walking, while separate preclinical projects explore brain-controlled spinal stimulation and directing spared pathways toward useful targets.
projects.stage: Human rehabilitation and separate preclinical programs

scale.metric: Voluntary function and durability of improvement
scale.detail: Measure what a participant can do with and without stimulation, and after training ends. Stimulation contact count does not specify restored dexterity, independence, or retained recovery.

translation.detail: Distinguish electrical stimulation that enables voluntary activity from stimulation that directly evokes a movement. A participant’s striking improvement is not a uniform outcome for all injuries; the 2024 report explicitly describes nonresponders.

labs.nextQuestion: Which physiological and injury characteristics predict useful gains, and which gains persist in daily life after assisted training?

sources.title: UW Medicine — Chet Moritz and research programs

labs.name: Neuromorphic Cognitive Systems
labs.summary: Indiveri’s group develops computing hardware inspired by the physical organization of nervous systems. Its work is relevant to neuroengineering through efficient event-driven processing and adaptive sensory-motor systems. The group studies artificial silicon neurons and synapses; these should not be confused with electrodes recording biological neurons.
labs.approach: Hybrid analogue and digital VLSI circuits implement neural dynamics, while asynchronous communication carries spike-like events between components. Local learning rules and recurrent network motifs support adaptation. The research connects circuit design with models of how embodied systems process information and select actions.

projects.title: Learning silicon neural circuits
projects.detail: The group designs low-power neuron and dynamic-synapse circuits, including spike-timing-dependent learning and competitive recurrent networks. These components test how adaptation can be implemented within the computing substrate instead of relying only on externally trained software models.

projects.title: Scalable asynchronous processors
projects.detail: The 2024 DYNAP-SE2 paper describes a mixed-signal processor with asynchronous event routing. Its circuits emulate mechanisms including short-term plasticity, adaptation and conductance-based dendritic compartments, allowing researchers to build and test dynamic spiking networks for real-time sensory processing.

scale.detail: Hardware scale should be assessed through computation, communication and adaptation costs. Silicon neuron counts, when reported, are not counts of neurons simultaneously observed in a brain.

translation.detail: The intended applications include real-time sensory-motor systems that interact with their environment using internal state and goals. The cited work describes computing research, not a clinical neural implant or approved treatment.

labs.nextQuestion: Editorial question: Which local learning mechanisms remain stable and useful when neuromorphic processors must adapt continuously to changing real-world sensory inputs?

sources.title: DYNAP-SE2: a scalable multi-core dynamic neuromorphic asynchronous spiking neural network processor

labs.affiliation: University of Zurich and ETH Zurich, Institute of Neuroinformatics

labs.name: Biomedical Engineering Research Group
labs.summary: Wits’s Biomedical Engineering Research Group combines physiological measurement, signal processing, assistive technology, and practical prototypes. Its neural-engineering examples include EEG interfaces, eye-controlled systems, rehabilitation robotics, and analysis of movement-related disease signs.
labs.approach: The school lists David Rubin as group leader and researchers with complementary expertise in speech, rehabilitation, and BCI prosthetics. The portfolio shows a systems-building approach: combine accessible sensors, computation, and a useful output, then evaluate the particular function the prototype is intended to serve.

projects.title: Brainternet: EEG as a networked signal
projects.detail: A 2017 project supervised by Adam Pantanowitz connected an Emotiv EEG device to a Raspberry Pi and streamed measurements to a web interface. The school describes a one-way brain-to-internet connection and movement classification, not transmission of unrestricted thoughts.

projects.title: Assistive control and movement assessment
projects.detail: The group portfolio includes eye-controlled wheelchair and cursor systems, brain-controlled robotic-arm demonstrations, and machine learning on spiral drawings to investigate Parkinson’s disease versus essential tremor. These are separate prototypes and analysis projects.

scale.metric: Accessible sensing and functional task performance
scale.detail: Relevant measures include control reliability, usability, and classification validity. The group page does not report a common patient cohort, current EEG-channel count, or validated diagnostic accuracy across these projects.

translation.detail: The program emphasizes assistive and biomedical applications. The public examples establish research and training prototypes; routine clinical deployment and disease diagnosis are not demonstrated by these pages.

labs.nextQuestion: Which low-cost sensing and control choices retain reliability for users whose movement or attention varies from day to day?

sources.title: Can you read my mind? Brainternet report, 2017

labs.name: Brain–Machine Intelligence and Qiushi BCI Research
labs.summary: Zhejiang’s public sources show a connected research environment spanning machine intelligence, implanted motor interfaces, and feedback stimulation. The computer-science laboratory directory names Gang Pan, Yueming Wang, and Yu Qi; the Qiushi Academy and affiliated hospital provide a separate clinical collaboration within the university.
labs.approach: The technical range includes learning algorithms that interpret brain activity and bidirectional systems that detect an abnormal neural state before applying stimulation. These are related research strands, not evidence that one device or team conducted every university BCI study.

projects.title: Implanted motor-interface collaboration
projects.detail: A February 2020 university report describes a 72-year-old participant controlling an external robotic arm and manipulator in three dimensions through an implanted interface. The report concerns a specific early clinical study rather than an established treatment service.

projects.title: Bidirectional epilepsy-control experiment
projects.detail: A 2014 paper involving Yu Qi and Yueming Wang coupled early seizure detection to cortical stimulation in a penicillin-induced rat epilepsy model. It reported 83% detection and a mean 3.11-second detection delay.

scale.detail: The rat study reported seizure duration reduced by an average 30.7% versus control. That endpoint is separate from the human motor-interface demonstration and cannot be used as a clinical epilepsy efficacy claim.

translation.detail: University–hospital collaboration provides a route from decoding research to human motor assistance. Animal feedback-stimulation results remain preclinical evidence.

labs.nextQuestion: Which decoding and stimulation methods remain reliable when behavior, neural signals, and clinical conditions change over months?

methodology: Start with university, department, institute, and center pages to find research groups across engineering, medicine, and neuroscience. Follow those pages to lab programs and selected primary studies.

For each profile, identify the investigators, concrete projects, methods, measured signals, and study setting. Distinguish platform aims from demonstrated findings and human studies from animal, ex-vivo, or computational work.

Attach references to the overview, each project, the progress measure, and the interpretation of evidence. Prefer official academic sources and original research; undated pages do not receive invented publication dates.

Treat progress measures and notebook questions as editorial synthesis. Electrode sites, simultaneous channels, isolated neurons, stimulation selectivity, functional recovery, and software adoption are different quantities.
Keep original atlas identifiers and link reviewed matches to the detailed profiles. University directories are discovery routes, not claims that every group on a roster has received a profile.
